papers.title: Water-Balance Physics-Informed Neural Network for Daily Streamflow Prediction: A Single-Catchment Comparative Study Using CAMELS-GB v2
papers.abstract: Accurate daily streamflow prediction remains challenging because rainfall–runoff dynamics are nonlinear, temporally dependent, and subject to water-mass conservation. This study examines whether a simplified catchment water-balance constraint improves the internal consistency of a physics-informed neural network (WB-PINN) without compromising predictive accuracy. Using 18,993 daily observations (1970–2022) from Catchment 31010 in CAMELS-GB v2, the WB-PINN jointly estimates discharge, latent storage, and an evapotranspiration scaling factor. Its loss function combines prediction error with a water-balance residual weighted by λ. We evaluated performance on a chronological independent test period (2012–2022) against Ridge regression, support vector regression, XGBoost, a multilayer perceptron, and an LSTM. We tested five physics-loss weights and additional regularization controls to distinguish physical constraints from generic regularization effects. At λ = 0.001, mean validation water-balance loss decreased from 13.69 to 8.22, with nearly unchanged accuracy (NSE 0.8419 versus 0.8433 without the constraint). On the test set, LSTM performed best (NSE 0.8673; RMSE 0.3772 mm/day), while WB-PINN ranked second numerically (NSE 0.8209; RMSE 0.4381 mm/day). Paired bootstrap analysis found no statistically significant differences between WB-PINN and XGBoost or support vector regression, whereas LSTM achieved lower RMSE and higher NSE. Removing antecedent discharge reduced accuracy across all models. Because storage and actual evapotranspiration were unobserved, reduced residuals do not establish hydrological realism. Test-period diagnostics revealed a persistent mean water-balance residual of −0.7070 mm/day and predicted evapotranspiration substantially below the long-term water-balance estimate. Thus, weak water-balance regularization reduced the imposed residual with little loss of predictive accuracy but did not achieve close water-balance closure or outperform the strongest data-driven model.

papers.title: Differentiable Contact Dynamics for Legged Locomotion: Policy Learning and Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion. The exact contact sensitivity is available in closed form but describes changes within the current contact mode, providing no first-order information toward neighboring contact modes. The proposed gradient replaces this sensitivity only in the backward pass, leaving the hard-contact forward solve unchanged and the realized rollout feasible. A central-path relaxation of the de Saxcé-corrected second-order-cone complementarity problem for Coulomb friction smooths the conditions defining the separating, clamping, and sliding modes. The relaxed sensitivity is evaluated at a point on the central path obtained by a Newton iteration initialized from the hard-contact solution. The sensitivity remains continuous through contact-mode transitions and converges to the exact sensitivity as the relaxation vanishes. Using 100,000 samples and less than 2 min of training on a desktop PC, policy learning with the proposed gradient produces a policy that transfers to hardware without fine-tuning. On hardware, the robot under a trotting policy withstands pushes and traverses debris and slippery ground. In trajectory optimization, the proposed gradient reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients. Project page: https://diffcontact.github.io

papers.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
papers.abstract: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.

papers.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller facilitates active learning for the critic by sampling continuations from states that are expected to most reduce the critic's estimation error. These refined value estimates then score the segment between consecutive states with a TD($λ$) advantage, while the sampled evidence supplies training targets for the critic. FOCUS supports long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning through a modular context-management interface that decouples context management from rollout allocation. Our experiments show that using compaction-induced segment boundaries for value estimation and credit assignment, FOCUS outperforms GRPO and VinePPO with matched per-step generation budgets on legal reasoning, deep search, and code localization benchmarks, improving held-out accuracy at Qwen3.5-9B scale by 7.2 points over the strongest baseline on BrowseComp-Plus (55.4 vs. 48.2) and by 4.1 points on DeonticBench (56.5 vs. 52.4).

papers.title: LUCID: Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with Conditional Density Estimation
papers.abstract: Computing local-level variable importance (VI) is critical for understanding machine learning models. Local permutation-based VI metrics offer a simple yet powerful approach, measuring how much a model's output changes when perturbing its inputs. However, existing perturbation strategies often ignore feature dependence or account for it only through restricted approximations. Perturbing a feature without fully respecting this dependence can generate unrealistic counterfactuals, thereby evaluating the model in regions unsupported by the observed data distribution. We address this gap by introducing a new model-agnostic local VI metric and estimator, Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with conditional Density estimation (LUCID). LUCID perturbs features of interest using plausible values drawn from the full conditional distribution given the remaining observed features. We establish theoretical connections between LUCID and existing VI measures, and provide an estimator with convergence guarantees and uncertainty quantification. Finally, we demonstrate LUCID's stable performance and practical utility across simulated and real-world examples.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
papers.abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency. Then, we design routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward. Finally, we consider trajectory selection as another approach to mitigate objective conflict, and design a kernel surrogate trajectory attribution algorithm that estimates how feedback signals from a set of trajectories influence policy learning on other trajectories. The kernel can capture nonlinear interactions such as synergy and antagonism between trajectories. We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.

papers.title: Active Learning of Conditional Generative Models via the Transport Neural Tangent Kernel
papers.abstract: Many high-throughput scientific experiments produce distributional outputs, requiring conditional generative models to interpret the data, and to predict outcomes at new inputs. Acquiring experimental data at new conditions (e.g., for a new antigen or a new cell type) is often expensive, motivating the need for automated experimental design methods. However, existing active learning frameworks are limited as they assume scalar or vector-valued outputs. We first show that the Wasserstein test risk of a conditional generative task decomposes into a mean term and a shape term, demonstrating why mean-based active learning is blind to distributional shape. To capture both, we propose the transport Neural Tangent Kernel (tNTK), a tractable kernel that measures how sensitive a generative model's predicted distribution is with respect to its parameters. The tNTK recovers the standard NTK in the deterministic limit and upper-bounds the posterior Fréchet variance of the prediction under small parameter perturbations. It admits a closed-form expression for affine Gaussian transport and tractable Monte Carlo estimators otherwise. Treating the tNTK as the covariance function of a Gaussian process, we greedily select inputs that minimize the total GP posterior variance across the pool, yielding a distribution-aware active learning strategy. We evaluate this strategy across four classes of conditional generative models, including conditional flow matching and conditional Monge gap, on synthetic distributions, intent-labeled sentences, and single-cell perturbation responses. In these experiments, the tNTK outperforms the baseline NTK computed from the conditional mean, demonstrating the value of distribution-aware active learning for generative-modeling tasks.

papers.title: Adapt for Planning, Not just Prediction: Optimistic Test-Time World Model Adaptation
papers.abstract: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this degradation by updating the model during deployment. Unlike pre-training on fixed data, TTA for planning is closed-loop: the planner uses model rollouts to select actions, and the resulting transitions drive the next update. This raises the question: which objective should guide TTA for planning? Under a prediction-only objective, the model is fit only to the outcomes of its own actions, so it can remain wrong about the actions that would reach the goal, and low prediction error need not translate into better planning. Inspired by reward-biased maximum likelihood from adaptive control, we introduce Optimistic Test-Time Adaptation (OpTTA). Its objective has two terms, the prediction loss on observed transitions and the planner's goal-reaching cost on its candidate rollouts, both minimized over the model parameters. The planning term biases adaptation toward models that are optimistic about reaching the goal, without any additional environment interaction. Across visual and environment shifts on manipulation, reaching and navigation tasks, OpTTA raises final planning success over the frozen model by 13.5 percentage points on average, compared with 6.9 for the prediction-only objective (AdaJEPA), when only the predictor is adapted. When the encoder is adapted as well, the gains are 13.5 and 7.5 points. These experiments span three JEPA world models with different encoders and training objectives and, for temporal straightening, both CEM and gradient-based planners. Our results suggest that test-time adaptation of world models for planning benefits from an optimistic, task-aware term in addition to the prediction loss.

papers.title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
papers.abstract: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. We present a distributed predictive flocking controller in which each robot solves its own nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem, optimizing swarm cohesion and alignment costs, inter-robot and obstacle safety, and a task objective, while exchanging only predicted trajectories with local neighbors. Within this generalized controller architecture, solved in real time, we compare six barrier and control-barrier-function (CBF) safety formulations on a digital twin of an open-source vibration-driven bristlebot in a $0.64\,\mathrm{m^2}$ arena. A look-ahead discrete-time CBF performs best overall, with the fewest collisions and the widest inter-robot margins across nearly every swarm size tested. We deploy it on phototaxis, phototactic orbiting, and cohesion without a stimulus tasks, using swarm sizes starting from ten robots and up to the geometric packing limit. The swarm holds well: collisions stay low in small swarms, rising steeply as the packing limit approaches, while coordination and cohesion degrade gently rather than collapsing. The swarm is found not to trade safety for order, keeping both across the confined arena, with local alignment high at every swarm size.

papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Training Reshapes Uncertainty Decomposition in Atomistic Models
papers.abstract: Multi-fidelity training, which combines abundant low-fidelity data with scarce high-fidelity labels, is increasingly common in atomistic modeling, but its effect on predictive uncertainty remains largely unexplored. We investigate this question using deep ensembles of mean-variance MACE models trained on ANI-1x, contrasting high-fidelity training from scratch with low-fidelity pretraining followed by fine-tuning. We characterize aleatoric, epistemic, and total uncertainty throughout training and under two distribution shifts: unseen molecular systems and higher-energy configurations. We find that pretraining reduces prediction error and improves uncertainty-based ranking across all test sets, but does not yield well-calibrated predictive variances; calibration deteriorates more severely under energy extrapolation. Training-dynamics analysis localizes most of this calibration degradation to high-fidelity optimization, during which the learned aleatoric variance becomes overconfident on held-out data. Moreover, multi-fidelity fine-tuning produces a more effective uncertainty-based acquisition function than high-fidelity training from scratch. These findings show that uncertainty ranking and calibration capture distinct properties and must be assessed separately in multi-fidelity atomistic models, especially under extrapolation.

papers.title: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization reveals HiPIMS deposition rates exceeding direct current sputtering
papers.abstract: Pulsed sputter processes are essential for a wide range of applications from hard coatings to microelectronics. High power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) offers unique possibilities for process design due to its high ionized flux fraction. Because of the high peak-current densities involved, correspondingly high plasma densities generate many ions. This enables tuning of kinetic energies by applying accelerating bias potentials. However, some HiPIMS processes have low deposition rates due to the back-attraction these ions experience with the negatively charged sputter target. Recent work in HiPIMS has targeted this problem, exploring complex pulsing schemes such as bipolar, multi-pulse, or chopped HiPIMS. These pulsing schemes introduce another problem: process complexity. As such, the process space, even with coarse intervals quickly blows up to 1E5-1E20 possible process combinations. This calls for efficient and intelligent sampling, which can be enabled by machine-learning algorithms such as Bayesian optimization. In this work we use multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) to efficiently sample the process space of pulse-packets, targeting high ionization flux fractions and deposition rates. Over 2,000 distinct processes were sampled during this exploration. Surprisingly, we found that many HiPIMS processes, including single pulse, can achieve deposition rates higher than DC references. In fact, at a working pressure of 1.0 Pa and moderate ionization rates of 5-20% we found that ms-scale pulses were ideal. We hypothesize these processes maximize gas rarefaction, creating a low-collision channel between the target and the substrate. These results showcase previously unreported behavior of pulsed sputter processes and challenge a long-held trade-off between film quality and speed in thin-film manufacturing.

papers.title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
papers.abstract: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes. We show that this memory is capacity-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and that its access set is known before compute, because the camera pose is an input. An analytical model built on these observations predicts spill points to within one chunk and classifies zero versus non-zero stalls correctly on held-out configurations. Guided by it, WorldPager stores int4 KV in a GPU/DRAM/NVMe hierarchy instead of recomputing it, prefetches each chunk's memory from the extrapolated pose, never waits on a miss, and writes back in the background; to our knowledge, it is the first to place the KV memory of an interactive world model on an NVMe tier with zero-stall prefetching. With training-free position handling, it generates 37.5 minutes of video continuously with zero stalls and constant host memory, at about 9.5 frames per second. On a sealed test set, int4 storage shows no measurable quality loss; on long-gap revisits it lowers image quality by about one MUSIQ point.

papers.title: Query Complexity of Learning Axis-Aligned Partitions
papers.abstract: This work establishes the query complexity of learning high-dimensional boxes in the exact query learning setting. Let $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of $n$ points, labeled by a collection of $k$ boxes: the label of each point in $X$ is determined by the unique box containing it. A learner aims to exactly recover the labels for every point in $X$ given access to a label oracle. We consider three increasingly-structured settings. In the most general setting, there are no conditions on the boxes, and they may overlap. We show that CAL (Cohn-Atlas-Ladner 1994), a classical active learning algorithm, is minimax-optimal with query complexity $Θ(kd \log (n/kd))$. When the boxes are disjoint, we examine two regimes. In the large-$k$ regime, CAL remains minimax-optimal. For the constant-$k$ regime, an optimized variant of the Halving algorithm (Hegedüs 1995) can beat CAL by a $\log(d)$ factor. Finally, in the most-structured settings, the boxes correspond to the leaves of a constant-sized decision tree. We prove a tight query complexity of $Θ(d + \log n)$ that is additive in $d$ and $\log n$, generalizing a recent result (Black-Larsen-Mazumdar-Saha-So 2026) that establishes the query complexity of learning decision stumps.

papers.title: Enhancing Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Motion Planning via Task Decomposition
papers.abstract: Training robotic manipulation policies in simulation is widely adopted due to safety and cost efficiency; however, tasks involving obstacles remain under-performing and often converge slowly under Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). To address this challenge, we propose a task decomposition framework for DRL that integrates Transfer Learning (TL) with Reward Redesign (RR) to improve learning efficiency and robustness in obstacle environments. The TL strategy selectively transfers only the first-layer critic parameters across structurally related tasks, since that layer captures general state--action representations while deeper layers encode reward- and obstacle-specific value geometry; RR decomposes tasks into staged sub-objectives to provide denser optimization signals. Experiments on the PyBullet Panda platform show consistent gains in obstacle settings. On Push with obstacle, our method achieves $0.83 \pm 0.05$, outperforming the strongest baseline (Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC), $0.77 \pm 0.06$) by approximately $7.8\%$. On Slide with obstacle, performance reaches $0.95 \pm 0.02$, exceeding Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) ($0.84 \pm 0.06$) by about $11\%$ success rates. In addition to higher final performance, forward transfer reduces convergence time by up to $70\%$ in obstacle tasks, and RR shortens sparse-reward Pick-and-Place training from roughly $0.75$M to $0.20$M steps ($\approx73\%$ reduction). The best policy is deployed on a real Franka Emika FR3 robot as a qualitative feasibility demonstration.

papers.title: An Interactive Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization Algorithm Based on Interpretable Active Preference Learning
papers.abstract: Many decision-making tasks are inherently multi-objective. Interactive evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms (iEMOAs) are particularly well-suited to help the decision-maker find their most preferred solution. However, many of these algorithms employ black-box preference models. For high-stakes decision-making tasks, like healthcare and defense, a high level of transparency is needed, for instance to support accountability. We propose an interpretable iEMOA which uses active learning to efficiently learn a tree-based preference model directly from pairwise comparisons. The survival operator of NSGA-II and NSGA-III is extended with the learned preference model to guide the algorithm towards the region of interest. An extensive experimental study compares the proposed method to a state-of-the-art black-box model and a state-of-the-art interpretable model. Results indicate that our proposed model outperforms the alternatives in terms of finding the most preferred solution at the cost of a slightly worse average final population. Finally, a case study on a real-life engineering problem illustrates how inspecting the learned model reveals which objectives drive the decision-maker's preferences.

papers.title: Benchmarking uncertainty quantification for engineering regression under graded distribution shift
papers.abstract: Machine learning models in engineering are often used beyond their training conditions, where reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) matters most. Existing comparisons of regression UQ methods rely on random splits, which assess calibration only in distribution. We introduce a three-rung shift ladder (in distribution, soft shift and hard shift) built along physically meaningful shift variables, and evaluate 12 methods from five families on seven public engineering datasets: five extrapolation settings, an unseen turbofan fault mode and a winter air-quality sensor deployment. All tuning uses source data only. In distribution, conformal methods cover at least 0.946 of test points on every dataset. Under hard shift, mean coverage falls to 0.40-0.75 across the 11 methods that always return an interval, and no systematic difference in method ranks is detected (Friedman p = 0.63). Weighted conformalised quantile regression stays near nominal on the points it answers, but abstains on 85\% of hard-shift points on average and covers only 0.67 of the few Concrete points it answers. Source-validation gains predict improvement in distribution and under soft shift, but not under hard shift (Spearman's rho = 0.04). Engineering evaluations should split calibration data by deployment unit, report subgroup coverage and sharpness, and treat abstention as an explicit operational outcome.

papers.title: Should Pseudo-Labels Share Mini-Batches with Labeled Examples? Semi-Supervised Continual Active Learning with Limited Training Cost
papers.abstract: Active learning (AL) reduces annotation by querying informative examples. Continual active learning (CAL) also cuts the training cost, the total number of gradient steps, by training one model across AL rounds with a fixed number of mini-batch steps per round. Pseudo-labels add supervision without annotation, but they increase training cost. In CAL, where every round trains on a fixed number of mini-batches, whether and how pseudo-labeled examples should share these mini-batches with labeled examples is therefore open. We provide the first formalization of this problem as two decisions after each query, namely (i) which unlabeled examples should enter training with a pseudo-label and (ii) what share of each mini-batch they should take. Our method, semi-supervised continual active learning (SSCAL), works with any acquisition function. It admits pseudo-labels based on distances from unlabeled examples to labeled neighbors, caps their share, and reweights the loss on labeled examples to keep their expected gradient contribution unchanged. On frozen embeddings, its pseudo-labeler updates incrementally without extra model forward passes. Across two audio datasets, two frozen encoders, six acquisition functions and ten seeds, SSCAL ranks first on average among four protocols with equal training steps, answering the question affirmatively.

papers.title: VisGeo-PipeTrack: A Visual Geometric Servo Control Framework with MPC-RCAPID Control for UAV-Based Dynamic Pipes Tracking
papers.abstract: While unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed for pipeline inspection, prevailing research predominantly assumes static pipes. In real-world industrial environments, pipes often exhibit dynamic movements, such as vibrations. This imposes more stringent requirements on UAVs' adaptive control and computational efficiency than in static scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes a servo control framework named VisGeo-PipeTrack, which utilizes geometric constraints to enable UAV tracking of dynamic pipes. To achieve efficient UAV positioning, YOLOv5 is employed to detect labels on the pipe. The positions are derived from visual geometric constraints based on these detected labels to enable precise localization. To address tracking control challenges, a model predictive control based real-time corrected adaptive PID (MPC-RCAPID) controller is proposed. papers.title: Geometric Consistency Based Label-Free Validation for Checkpoint Selection in Audio Active Learning
papers.abstract: Audio active learning (AL) trains a classifier at low annotation cost by labeling only an informative fraction of an unlabeled collection over successive rounds. Each round picks one of the checkpoints saved during training. Mainstream AL protocols do so with an assumed validation set, but in practice its labels also count toward the annotation cost, shrinking the advantage of an already small annotation budget. We propose geometric consistency, a label-free validation rule for checkpoint selection. Both classifiers, nearest-class-mean and k-nearest-neighbor, are built from the labeled set in a frozen pretrained embedding space. They then predict the unlabeled data to model its geometry. The rule scores each checkpoint by its agreement with these pseudo-labels and its cross-entropy on the labeled set. It works with any query strategy, has one hyperparameter, insensitive in practice, and adds only one batched forward pass over the unlabeled data per round. At matched label budgets across datasets, encoders, and query strategies, it attains the best mean rank in area under the labeling curve (AULC) among methods without extra labels and is on par with an out-of-budget validation set. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of label-free validation for checkpoint selection in audio AL.

papers.title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
papers.abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a $(1+1)$ evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.

papers.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

papers.abstract: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) extends conformal prediction beyond the coverage setting to the control of general monotone loss functions, in a distribution-free and modelagnostic fashion. This makes it well-suited to problems with high-dimensional targets, such as the semantic segmentation task addressed in this work. However, CRC guarantees only marginal control, meaning that the risk is controlled on average over the data distribution. Under imbalanced distributions, the risk on inputs that contain rare objects may therefore remain uncontrolled, even when the marginal guarantee holds. We propose a new method that controls the risk on average over user-defined groups of the domain, drawing on Mondrian conformal prediction and macro-coverage algorithms. The method relies on a taxonomy, that is, a function that assigns a group to each data point, and reweights each point's risk by a coefficient that depends on its group probability, so that rare points contribute more than common ones. We illustrate the approach on two semantic segmentation datasets.

papers.title: Learning Direct Control from Optimization for Dynamic Target Tracking
papers.abstract: Dynamic target tracking requires a mobile robot to maintain target visibility while navigating obstacles with smooth, feasible controls. Online trajectory optimization explicitly encodes these objectives but requires repeated numerical solving, whereas waypoint-based neural policies separate geometric prediction from control execution. We introduce LECO, a framework that transfers tracking optimization into offline learning of a direct-control policy. LECO predicts control sequences and maps them to trajectories through a differentiable kinematic model, allowing trajectory-level objectives to directly guide control learning. A decaying expert-guidance curriculum initializes effective tracking behavior and progressively shifts learning toward these task objectives. At deployment, a predictive safety lock checks short-horizon obstacle clearance and invokes a classical planning and control fallback when the predicted motion is unsafe or the target prediction is invalid. Across three simulated obstacle densities, LECO reduces root-mean-square linear jerk by 14.1--31.2\% relative to the best competing method for this metric and achieves the highest tracking success rate, with per-cycle computation times of 4.25--5.63\,ms. Experiments on two robot platforms further demonstrate tracking through indoor narrow passages and outdoor forest environments. These results demonstrate that learning direct control from optimization enables smooth and robust dynamic target tracking.

papers.title: Physics-Informed and Data-Driven Composite Disturbance Separation and Predictive Control for Airborne Electro-Optical Gimbals with Multiple Constraints

Under carrier vibration, input delay, and actuator constraints, achieving line-of-sight stabilization and tracking is challenging. A disturbance-separated model predictive control (MPC) scheme is proposed to compensate these heterogeneous disturbances according to their physical characteristics. An adaptive periodic observer predicts multi-harmonic vibrations over the MPC horizon using linear-regression frequency estimation. A linear observer estimates the aperiodic disturbance, and a bounded long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts its change over the input delay. Embedding periodic predictions into the MPC model while applying aperiodic compensation outside the optimizer limits amplification of aperiodic estimation errors and improves pointing accuracy under frequency changes and parameter mismatch. On the stated headroom envelope, input-set tightening provides feasible commands within the prescribed limits, and a regional practical tracking bound is established under explicit input-sequence and predicted-state margin conditions. A UAV-mounted two-axis gimbal platform is assembled for comparative indoor hovering experiments, complemented by simulations under frequency changes and parameter mismatch. In the reported trials, the proposed method achieves yaw and pitch relative-angle root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 0.770 degrees and 0.350 degrees, reducing tracking errors by 25.1% and 45.9% compared with linear active disturbance rejection control.

papers.title: Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
papers.abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation (0.0086 +/- 0.0002) mu_B/Mn that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of (291 +/- 2) K.

A hybrid rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) transmission scheme is further designed to improve spectral efficiency. We formulate an energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing transmit beamforming, power and rate allocation, MM-RIS configurations, panel deployment, and ME positions. To address the resulting non-convex mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem, we propose constrained hybrid deep reinforcement learning with federated transformer and parametrized sharing (CRAFTS). CRAFTS integrates multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) and multi-agent deep Q-networks (MADQN) through bi-directional parametrized sharing to handle continuous and discrete actions, respectively. Moreover, a transformer-based architecture and federated learning (FL) are incorporated to enhance state representation and distributed knowledge sharing, whilst a Lagrangian-based adaptive penalty mechanism facilitates the constraint satisfaction. Simulation results have demonstrated that the proposed MM-RIS architecture and CRAFTS framework substantially improve EE and constraint satisfaction compared to the benchmarks in the open literature. Moreover, the results validate the benefits of spatially reconfigurable MM-RIS, hybrid RSMA-NOMA transmissions, and intelligent collaborative learning, highlighting the potential of the proposed framework for energy-efficient and adaptive next-generation wireless networks.

papers.abstract: Assistive agents in shared-control settings face a dual challenge: acting proactively to align with the human's intentions while remaining legible enough for the human to comprehend and fluently respond in real time. We present Dream2Assist, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for tightly-coupled shared decision making that addresses both sides of this challenge. Our approach extends a recurrent state-space world model with intent inference, enabling an assistive policy trained via fictitious co-play to anticipate and support discrete human objectives without overriding human agency. Beyond the computational framework, we describe the full deployment pipeline needed to translate a world-model-based policy into a safe, human-centered system in a resource-efficient way. Crucially, we address the sim-to-real-human gap via policy down-selection and reward restructuring within an iterative human-machine interface design. We validate the framework through three human-subjects studies and a preliminary on-vehicle deployment spanning two qualitatively distinct domains: high-speed racing (N=30) and urban driving with richer intent structure (N=10). Our results demonstrate that intent conditioning yields measurable improvements in torque alignment and collision rate. We surface key design insights and practices for deploying learning-based assistive agents in safety-critical, real-time human-robot teaming.

papers.title: Generalized anxiety disorder may lead to increased healthcare utilization following total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Psychiatric comorbidities are increasingly recognized as modifiers of arthroplasty outcomes. However, the effect of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) on outcomes following total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains underexplored. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the PearlDiver national database to identify patients who underwent primary, unilateral THA for osteoarthritis between 2010 and 2022. Patients with <90-day follow-up were excluded. Among 278,655 eligible patients, 17,422 (6.2%) had a preoperative diagnosis of GAD. These patients were propensity score-matched 1:1 (caliper 0.2) to patients without GAD, resulting in 34,844 matched THAs. Primary outcomes included 90-day emergency department (ED) visits, readmissions, reoperations, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) at 90 days, 1 and 2 years, and revision procedures at 1 and 2 years. Annual trends in GAD prevalence among THA patients were also analyzed. Results GAD was associated with significantly increased odds of 90-day ED visits (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.21; 95% CI, 1.13–1.29; P <0.001) and 90-day reoperations (AOR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.05–1.37; P =0.006). No differences were observed in readmissions, PJI, or revision rates at any time point. GAD prevalence among THA patients rose from 0.54% in 2010 to 10.14% in 2022—a 19-fold increase ( R 2 =0.99, P <0.001). Conclusion Preoperative GAD is associated with higher risk of 90-day ED visits and reoperations following THA. The rising prevalence of GAD suggests that preoperative mental health status may be relevant to perioperative risk stratification and supports further study of targeted optimization strategies in patients undergoing THA.

papers.title: Biomechanical performance of zygomatic and pterygoid implants in the rehabilitation of the severely atrophic maxilla: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Zygomatic and pterygoid implants are reliable graft less options for severely atrophic maxilla rehabilitation. These implant configurations have been explored in many finite element and experimental biomechanical investigations; however, the evidence is scattered, and a systematic review has not been done to analyze their biomechanical performance to thoroughly assess the biomechanical performance of zygomatic and pterygoid implants for severely atrophic maxillae. The systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251130553). We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar since database establishment to June 2026. Stress distribution, strain, implant displacement, micromotion, load transfer, prosthetic framework stress, and peri-implant bone stress were assessed using finite element models and experimental biomechanical tests. Methodological quality was assessed using the ROBFEAD and QUIN tool of risk assessment Thirteen studies were included. Most were finite element analyses, with 2 biomechanics experiments. While isolated zygomatic implants had lower peri-implant stress than pterygoid implants, coupled zygomatic-pterygoid implants improved posterior load transfer, cantilever effects, biomechanical stability, and implant micromotion. The available biomechanical evidence suggests that implant distribution and posterior support may substantially influence mechanical behavior under simulated loading conditions. Combined zygomatic-pterygoid configurations generally demonstrated more favorable load sharing, reduced cantilever-related stress and lower micromotion in the investigated models. However, these findings represent relative biomechanical trends derived predominantly from computational simulations and should not be interpreted as evidence of superior clinical survival or treatment success. Standardized biomechanical studies and prospective clinical investigations are required to determine their clinical relevance.

papers.title: Risk-informed credibility goals for finite element simulation of rib bone plates: a case study in applying ASME V&V 40 to ASTM F382 testing
papers.abstract: Introduction While Computational Modeling and Simulation (CM&S) holds significant potential as key evidence in the design and regulatory approval process for medical devices, establishing the credibility of these results remains paramount. This study presents a case study applying the ASME V&V 40 risk-based framework to the evaluation of the four-point bending performance of rib bone plates. Methods We established two distinct Contexts of Use (COUs) for a Class III rib bone plate. COU 1 (Design Change) utilizes CM&S as stand-alone evidence for a design change (increasing the number of holes), corresponding to a High-Medium model risk. Conversely, COU 2 (Product Line Extension) employs CM&S as supplementary evidence for product line expansion (varying bending shapes), corresponding to a Medium-Medium model risk. To meet the credibility requirements commensurate with each COU, we systematically performed Numerical Code Verification (NCV), calculation verification (discretization and solver errors), sensitivity analysis, Uncertainty Quantification (UQ), and validation of the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) model using ASTM F382 bench testing. Results Verification activities confirmed numerical stability with an NCV error of 0.704%. Validation results demonstrated that the FE model agreed with experimental four-point bending results within 5% error. For key Quantities of Interest such as bending stiffness, the validation metric (|E|/Uval < 1) further supported model adequacy under the stated Context of Use. Discussion Consequently, in COU 1, where the Question of Interest (QOI) is whether increasing the hole count degrades performance, the model predicted a negligible impact (<0.2%), illustrating how CM&S may support regulatory decisions on such design changes; as this prediction was not accompanied by physical testing of the extended configurations, experimental confirmation would provide complementary evidence. In COU 2, where the QOI is whether the model can predict the performance of new pre-contoured shapes, errors within the 10% threshold established for this COU support the use of the model as supplementary evidence. This case study illustrates an approach to defining the role of CM&S based on risk and tailoring corresponding VVUQ activities to secure the credibility of data submitted for medical device regulations.

papers.title: DENTAL IMPLANTATION IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETES MELLITUS: RISK FACTORS, COMPLICATIONS, AND EVIDENCE-BASED CLINICAL MANAGEMENT
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is one of the most common chronic metabolic diseases encountered in dental practice, and its influence on wound healing, bone metabolism, immune defence, and infection control is directly relevant to implant dentistry. Contemporary evidence indicates that dental implant treatment can be safe and predictable in patients with well-controlled diabetes, whereas poor glycaemic control is associated with delayed osseointegration, greater marginal bone loss, peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis, and higher implant failure rates. This article reviews the principal risk factors for adverse outcomes, describes early and late complications, and summarises an evidence-based clinical pathway that includes medical assessment, optimisation of glycaemic control, rigorous periodontal and peri-implant maintenance, and coordinated physician-dentist management. Diabetes should therefore be regarded as a modifiable risk factor rather than an absolute contraindication to implant therapy.

papers.abstract: Strut-based lattice metamaterials exhibiting near-zero Poisson’s ratio (NZPR) behaviour have been identified as potential candidates for orthopaedic implants because of their limited lateral expansion and dimensional stability. This study presents a systematic, comparative evaluation of three previously reported honeycomb-based NZPR lattices, namely RSRE, P-ZPR, and SRE-1, and two novel honeycomb-based NZPR lattices, namely SRE-2 and SRE-3, relative to conventional body-centred cubic and face-centred cubic reference lattices, which exhibit positive Poisson’s ratios (PPR). The evaluation is performed within the context of bone tissue engineering, using load-bearing lumbar interbody fusion (LIF) as an exemplary application. Compressive behaviour, deformation mechanisms, Poisson’s ratio evolution, von Mises stress distribution, energy absorption, and morphological parameters were characterised through experimental investigations and finite element simulations. All NZPR lattices exhibited bending-dominated deformation with near-zero lateral strain, whereas SRE-type lattices displayed comparatively more homogeneous stress distributions than the other NZPR and PPR configurations. The P-ZPR lattice demonstrated superior compressive strength and energy absorption capacity, while RSRE and SRE-3 exhibited highly compliant mechanical responses with stable progressive collapse, though insufficient load-bearing capacity for use in primary structural components. Among the designs investigated, SRE-2 was the most promising for load-bearing LIF implants, offering an effective compromise between material consumption and mechanical performance, combined with controlled collapse behaviour and favourable morphological characteristics. Further, a qualitative basis for the initial rational selection of NZPR lattice configuration for bone tissue engineering applications was established.

papers.title: Stable 2-year migration on radiostereometric analysis and improved gait speed and function after bicruciate-retaining TKA: a prospective cohort of 25 patients
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In bicruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty (BCR TKA) the preservation of both cruciate ligaments necessitates a different tibial tray design with reduced bone-implant interface. These ligaments also influence knee joint force dynamics and may thereby affect component migration. The primary aim of our study was to assess the fixation of BCR TKA up to 2 years postoperatively. Secondary aims included the evaluation of clinical and functional outcomes. METHODS: This prospective study (https://osf.io/zqt8d) included 25 BCR TKA patients. Migration of both components was assessed at different follow-up time points by model-based radiostereometric analysis (RSA) using bone markers. Primary outcome was total translation (TT) and total rotation (TR) at the 2-year follow-up. Secondary outcomes included at-home gait parameters (gait speed, stride length, stride time) assessed with wearable sensors, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), and adverse events (AEs). RESULTS: At the 2-year follow-up, least-squares mean tibial TT was 0.22 mm (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.16-0.28) (tibia) and femoral TT 0.43 mm (CI 0.30-0.57). The least-squares mean tibial TR was 0.53° (CI 0.43-0.63) and femoral TR 0.64° (CI 0.46-0.82). PROMs improved significantly after surgery, with improvements exceeding the predefined minimal clinically important difference (MCID). Gait outcomes revealed a significant gait speed improvement, which remained below MCID, and no significant difference from healthy controls 1 year postoperatively. AEs included 2 intraoperative tibial eminence fractures, 4 cases of persistent postoperative pain, and 2 cases of postoperative oedema with temporary knee stiffness. CONCLUSION: RSA analysis of this BCR TKA demonstrated a stabilizing migration pattern that remained below established TKA benchmark values (for different designs), indicating good fixation at 2-year follow-up. The findings were accompanied by an improved PROM, whereas gait speed improvement was below MCID.

papers.title: Engineering predictive human-relevant models: biomaterials at the interface of biology and function
papers.abstract: Discovering pathophysiological pathways and disease treatments relies on access to human-relevant tissue models. Two-dimensional (2D) in vitro cultures and animal models remain foundational to biomedical research; however, 2D systems lack tissue-level complexity, and species-specific differences limit the translational fidelity of animal data. Addressing this gap requires a shift from biologically representative models towards functionally predictive systems capable of generating quantitative, physiologically meaningful readouts of human tissues. Biomaterials have emerged as the critical engineering interface enabling this shift, providing tuneable control over the biochemical, mechanical, and structural cues that govern cell fate and tissue function and dysfunction. In this perspective, we examine four converging domains advancing human-relevant modelling: biomaterial-based non-animal systems that reduce reliance on interspecies extrapolation; organ-on-chip platforms that recreate dynamic, multi-tissue physiological environments; and organoids and 3D bioprinting, which build living tissue complexity from self-organising or engineered cellular systems. Biomechanical validation approaches complete this picture, ensuring engineered constructs faithfully reproduce native tissue function rather than structure alone. We propose that their integration, rather than independent use, provides a framework for next-generation human-relevant models. The future of predictive human modelling lies not in biological complexity alone, but in the deliberate integration of material design, biological organisation, physiological function, and rigorous validation to generate human-relevant systems with greater translational value and reduced reliance on animal experimentation.

papers.title: Predicting in the Dark Room of Embeddings: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures, Latent-Space Geometry and World Models: A Companion Volume to Euclid in the Retrieval Engine
papers.abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting the representation of a hidden part of an input from the representation of a visible part, rather than reconstructing pixels or contrasting positive and negative pairs. This paper, a companion to the author's Euclid in the Retrieval Engine, gives a fresh, self-contained account of the JEPA family (I-JEPA for images, V-JEPA and V-JEPA 2 for video and action-conditioned planning, MC-JEPA for motion and content, and LeJEPA's provable regulariser), read through the energy-based view of learning. It sets out the three paradigms of self-supervised learning side by side, explains why predicting in latent space invites representational collapse, and compares the mechanisms that prevent it: stop-gradient with an exponential-moving-average target, variance–covariance regularisation, and distributional matching to an isotropic Gaussian. The paper then connects JEPA's latent geometry to the themes of the earlier volume. Normalisation, cosine and Euclidean distance, distance concentration and isotropy are not afterthoughts for a JEPA: they decide whether collapse is visible, whether its latent energy is meaningful, and whether its embeddings can serve visual retrieval. Three small computed experiments, written for this paper, show that a scale-invariant rank measure can miss total collapse, that centring and normalisation do not cure distance concentration in high dimensions, and that planning by minimising an L1 latent energy converges quickly in a toy world model. The paper closes with implications for visual retrieval-augmented generation, open questions and a calibrated verdict. Companion volume to Euclid in the Retrieval Engine (KSCCN series).

papers.title: Reconstructing Glacier Dynamics in Complex Terrain with ICESat-2 and Gaussian Process Interpolation
papers.abstract: Abstract. We apply Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to ICESat-2 along-track height change data to generate spatially continuous glacier height change fields across two glaciated regions with complex topography and dynamic behaviour: Larsen-B (Antarctic Peninsula) and central Southern Svalbard. For Larsen-B, GPR-derived height change rates from 2021–2024 average −0.61 ± 0.02 m a–1, corresponding to a volume loss of 4.55 ± 0.17 km³ a–1, similar to independent estimates from TanDEM-X. In Svalbard, we observe widespread thinning (−1.57 ± 0.03 m a–1) and detect clear signals of surging glaciers. GPR's multi-dimensional, uncertainty-aware framework enables accurate interpolation across data gaps and supports the detection of localized dynamic events, such as surges. Sensitivity tests show that interpolation errors increase with gap size, slope, and extrapolation distance. Our findings demonstrate that GPR is well-suited for enhancing the spatial and temporal resolution of altimetry-based glacier monitoring, enabling improved estimates of height and volume change while reconstructing spatially localized phenomena such as surge activity and other transient glacier dynamics.

papers.title: Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

papers.title: Drum-Buffer-Rope and rolling horizon MILP for shifting bottleneck synchronization in sugar beet logistics
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study develops and validates a cyber-physical mathematical framework for synchronizing stochastic agricultural harvesting with deterministic industrial processing in regional sugar beet logistics. The framework addresses real-time coordination conflicts between distributed field supply nodes, limited transport capacity, dynamic field accessibility, and continuous factory demand. Prior work: Traditional static logistics models treat agro-industrial cargo as inert mass and primarily optimize spatial distance. Such approaches are poorly suited to environments characterized by high-frequency schedule nervousness, weather-driven field accessibility changes, shifting bottlenecks, and non-linear raw material degradation during temporary field storage. Approach: The proposed Digital Twin architecture combines dynamic Drum-Buffer-Rope (DBR) pull logic for shifting bottlenecks with rolling Model Predictive Control (MPC) and a multi-phase Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) heuristic. Spatial transport work is handled during seasonal stratification, feasible route assignment, and topological filtering; within the active rolling MILP core it is treated as a quasi-invariant structural term. This allows the optimization layer to focus on time-sensitive trade-offs between sucrose preservation, factory starvation avoidance, and logistical feasibility. Results: Empirical validation using an 11- year industrial dataset comprising more than 180,000 unique transactional cycles shows that the multi-phase heuristic achieves sub-second solver response times in the tested industrial scenarios, with the active MILP core converging within 0.45 seconds. Operational deployment is associated with compression of factory reception-yard turnaround time from 24.6 to 13.8 minutes and a 41% reduction in active fleet dispersion. Implications: The adaptive sigmoid switching mechanism dynamically shifts objective priorities between quality preservation and plant starvation avoidance during environmental shocks. For practitioners, the framework provides a real-time execution tool for synchronizing harvesting, loading, transportation, and factory reception under stochastic disturbances. For researchers, it demonstrates a scalable approach to time- based buffer management in temporal agro-industrial networks. Value: The scientific novelty lies in integrating adaptive DBR pull constraints, rolling MILP optimization, graph-based topological filtering, and physics- informed quality inputs into a unified cyber-physical synchronization framework. The proposed architecture transforms agricultural logistics from a rigid cost center into a resilience-oriented decision system without compromising grower equity or systemic transparency.

papers.title: Multimodal Knowledge Transfer Framework for Cross-Cultural Dissemination of Henan's Historical and Cultural Heritage
papers.abstract: To address “cultural discount” and cognitive barriers in cross-cultural dissemination of Henan's historical heritage (oracle bone script, Longmen Grottoes, Shaolin Kung Fu), this study builds a multimodal knowledge transfer framework (linguistic, visual, auditory, interactive) based on multimodal translation, intercultural communication, and knowledge management. A descriptive-correlational design was employed, drawing on adapted survey responses from 22 public elementary school teachers. Frequencies, percentages, weighted means, and Pearson product–moment correlation coefficients were used to describe respondents’ characteristics, four dimensions of active-learning perceptions, four readiness dimensions, and their relationships with teacher profile variables. Respondents strongly agreed with the potential of technology-enabled active learning for interactive engagement (M = 4.68), problem-solving (M = 4.55), interest (M = 4.52), and feedback (M = 4.52). Readiness was highest in the attitudinal dimension (M = 4.66), followed by instructional (M = 4.22), pedagogical (M = 4.14), and technological readiness (M = 4.00). Training and seminars attended were significantly and positively related to perceptions (r = .47, p = .027) and readiness (r = .51, p = .016). Age, gender, educational attainment, and years of service had no statistically significant associations with either outcome in the reported analysis. These findings informed a proposed instructional supervision plan emphasizing hands-on technology training, peer coaching, classroom-focused feedback, and technical assistance. The findings reflect self-reported perceptions and associations rather than verified effects on student achievement.

papers.abstract: Knowledge management activities are an interest of health librarians in the UK, and the English national strategy for NHS Knowledge and Library Services has emphasized the role of knowledge broker for health librarians and information professionals. The aim of this study is to investigate library and information staff perceptions and attitudes toward their role in knowledge management and mobilization. A quantitative online survey was first piloted with the NHS England Knowledge Management Team and then sent out to NHS library and information professionals via four established networks. Responses (n = 72, estimated 33.3% response rate) indicated that prominent factors that influence the knowledge and library service role in informational and relational activities included service funding, capacity, feasibility of gaining new skills, senior management engagement, and perceived value of the services. Strategic policy documents for knowledge and library services need to highlight how to achieve some possible knowledge broker activities that would support better patient care.

papers.title: Bioengineering strategies for next-generation female reproductive organoids: A roadmap to clinical translation
papers.abstract: The human female reproductive system is characterized by highly dynamic tissue remodeling, cyclical endocrinology, and the precise orchestration of maternal–fetal immune tolerance. Historically, deciphering reproductive pathologies ranging from infertility to obstetric complications and malignancies has been hampered by the fundamental physiological and interspecies disparities inherent in 2D cultures and animal models. While three-dimensional (3D) organoid technology has initiated a paradigm shift, conventional static cultures relying on poorly defined, xenogeneic matrices (e.g., Matrigel) introduce profound immunogenic confounding factors and severe bioengineering bottlenecks. To bridge this gap, this review comprehensively delineates the advanced bioengineering strategies driving the next-generation of female reproductive models. We first outline foundational engineering pillars, highlighting the transition toward intelligent biomaterials, deterministic 3D bioprinting, and microfluidic microenvironments. Subsequently, we critically evaluate state-of-the-art organoid models across the ovary, fallopian tube, the maternal–fetal interface containing endometrium and placenta, cervix, and vagina. We emphasize how multi-lineage “assembloids” and multiorgan microphysiological systems successfully recapitulate transient implantation events and bidirectional endocrine crosstalk. Finally, we propose a strategic roadmap for the field, demonstrating how the integration of materials science, genetics, multi-omics, and engineering methods will overcome current limitations, ultimately accelerating the transition from benchtop in vitro models to standardized clinical diagnostics and reproductive regenerative therapeutics.

papers.title: A workflow-aligned framework for AI literacy in materials-informatics education: scientific judgment, equity, and curriculum design
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to predict materials properties, prioritize experiments, and generate hypotheses in materials science. The limiting challenge is no longer only algorithmic capability, but also whether students and educators can use AI with domain-specific scientific judgment. This conceptual analysis argues that AI education for AI-powered materials discovery should move beyond tool access and surface-level interaction with generative systems toward a workflow-aligned model of AI literacy. The analysis links AI literacy to core materials-informatics competencies: data provenance, domain-specific featurization, model validation, uncertainty quantification, physics-informed reasoning, reproducibility, and experimental feedback. It also advances an outcome-oriented equity perspective in which institutions evaluate not only access and participation, but also comparable learning gains, transfer of learning, learner confidence calibration, persistence, and research readiness across student subgroups. The article synthesizes relevant evidence, identifies cognitive and ethical risks such as off-loading and cognitive surrender, and proposes a dual-track curriculum model, implementation recommendations, reusable curriculum artifacts, and a set of testable propositions for future study. The central goal is to prepare students to become better scientists—not merely more efficient users of AI tools.

papers.title: Correlative SEM-EDS-XRD Characterization of Surface Modification in LPBF Inconel 718 after Wire Electrical Discharge Machining
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables near-net-shape production of Inconel 718 components, but electrically conductive post-processing is often required to obtain final dimensions and accessible cut surfaces. This study presents a before-after characterization of LPBF Inconel 718 subjected to one fixed wire electrical discharge machining (WEDM) condition. The comparison is intentionally limited to the available paired scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) dataset and does not claim process-parameter optimization. The pre-WEDM LPBF surface displayed heterogeneous relief, locally adhered material, and track-like surface features, whereas the WEDM-cut surface exhibited crater-like depressions, globular resolidified particles, adhered debris, and localized crack-like discontinuities. EDS showed marked near-surface compositional changes: oxygen increased from 0.66 to 9.13 wt.%, copper from 0.68 to 5.65 wt.%, and zinc changed from below detection to 3.89 wt.%, consistent with oxidation and transfer from the brass wire electrode. The elevated carbon signal after WEDM is treated cautiously because deionized water was used as the dielectric and the available dataset does not exclude preparation or surface-contamination artefacts. XRD retained the dominant facecentred cubic gamma-Ni reflections after machining; apparent peak-position changes were observed, but they are not interpreted quantitatively as residual stress because calibration and peak-fitting uncertainty were not available. The combined results indicate that the selected WEDM operation produced pronounced morphological and chemical modification of the near-surface region while preserving the dominant bulk matrix phase. The study provides a transparent baseline for subsequent quantitative work on roughness, recast-layer thickness, residual stress, fatigue, and corrosion.

papers.title: Designing a Gamified Tool: An ADDIE Approach to Capital Market Flashcard Development
papers.abstract: Traditional, lecture-based finance courses frequently overwhelm undergraduate students with dense theoretical content, leading to poor knowledge retention, lower overall engagement, and a heavy reliance on last-minute cramming before major assessments. To address these persistent educational challenges, this study details the design, development, and implementation of a mobile-friendly digital flashcard game specifically tailored for an undergraduate Financial Markets and Institutions (FIN) course using the systematic ADDIE instructional design framework. By integrating active recall strategies, custom visual aids, and an algorithm-driven Spaced Repetition System (SRS), the platform transforms passive studying into a dynamic learning process that prompts students to systematically review challenging concepts based on their individual mastery levels. Subject-matter experts rigorously vetted the curriculum content for accuracy and practical relevance prior to deployment, while formative evaluations directly measured student usability, overall engagement, and conceptual comprehension during active coursework. Formative findings, including high expert ratings for content validity and evidence of adaptive scheduling from system logs, suggest that the tool has strong potential to support active recall. However, its effectiveness in improving long-term knowledge retention and reducing academic anxiety will be examined in a subsequent summative evaluation. Ultimately, by documenting the comprehensive analysis, design, and development phases, this study provides instructional designers and finance educators with a practical, replicable blueprint for implementing gamified, technology-enhanced active learning tools across complex capital markets curricula.

These operational constraints make them unsuitable for daily industrial use. Particular focus is given to the practical challenges faced by manufacturers when implementing these approaches in real production conditions. papers.title: Optical tomography for in-situ quality assurance in laser powder bed fusion: From defect detection to closed-loop control: A critical review
papers.abstract: Abstract Metal additive manufacturing has become a disruptive manufacturing method for producing components in critical applications; therefore, quality assurance is increasingly important for ensuring part reliability and performance. Traditional methods for examining parts, such as destructive testing and X-ray computed tomography, can be costly, time-consuming, and impractical for inspecting every part in a production run. In-situ monitoring using optical tomography (OT) has gained increasing attention for quality control in processes such as laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) because it provides a relatively low-cost monitoring solution with relatively simple hardware integration into commercial systems for full-field, layer-wise monitoring of the build process. It covers the fundamental principles, sensor configurations, research trends, and applications for quality assurance and defect detection. The discussion addresses the challenges and limitations these systems face, such as data management, signal interpretation, and calibration. The review highlights future opportunities to apply OT with machine learning to create digital twins or enable closed-loop control, thereby improving reliable build strategies in metal additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Ontology-enabled neuro-symbolic closed-loop control of laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: A geometry-conditioned, neuro-symbolic closed-loop architecture is proposed for laser powder bed fusion, in which an ontology aligned with established standards and domain vocabularies operates inside the control loop and couples symbolic reasoning with statistical learning to set the targets of a constraint-aware predictive controller. The ontology links the process objectives and constraints to the signals a controller can observe. A description-logic reasoner selects the active constraints, which are converted into references and bounds enforced on each scan. The demonstrated case is overhang dross: a quality limit on the melt pool depth, which governs quality but is not measured in the present formulation, is mapped through a geometry- and power-dependent depth-to-width ratio onto a bound on the observable width. The ratio and its empirical uncertainty are estimated by a neural ensemble. The reasoner classifies each upcoming feature and selects the active constraints, adding a lack-of-fusion floor at overhangs and an extrapolation guard when the overhang angle falls below the calibrated range or uncertainty is high. It runs only when the symbolic context changes, and the inferred classification remains cached between changes. In an Eagar–Tsai surrogate calibrated to the NIST AM-Bench benchmark for IN625, the architecture reduced the mean total defect count at 45° from 6.0 to 6.2 tracks for the geometry-conditioned baselines to 3.2 per build and avoided their shift from dross to lack of fusion. Ablation attributed the ontology contribution to explicit representation of constraint applicability, inference, and consistency checking rather than separate numerical gains. The results establish architectural feasibility. Machine-specific calibration of the depth-to-width relation and physical validation are the principal next steps.
