papers.title: An Explainable and Optimized Ensemble Learning Framework Using XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM for Predictive Analytics
papers.abstract: AbstractPredictive analytics on complex tabular datasets is a cornerstone of data-driven decision-making across high-stakes domains including financial risk assessment, healthcare prognostics, and customer intelligence. Although Gradient Boosted Decision Tree (GBDT) architectures—predominantly XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM—exhibit superior empirical predictive power over deep neural networks on tabular structures, three foundational challenges persist: (1) high sensitivity to complex, non-convex hyperparameter spaces; (2) vulnerability to data leakage and validation bias; and (3) a notorious "black-box" opacity that impedes regulatory compliance and clinical adoption. This study proposes an explainable, Bayesian-optimized stacking ensemble learning framework that addresses these challenges systematically. The framework integrates XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM as heterogeneous base-level learners, rigorously tuned via Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization within an Optuna framework across 50 trials per algorithm under leakage-free nested 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Out-of-fold (OOF) predicted probability vectors are fed into an ElasticNet regularized logistic meta-learner to synthesize orthogonal decision boundaries. Experimental results on an empirical benchmark (N = 30,000) demonstrate that the proposed Stacking Meta-Ensemble outperforms all individual models (ROC-AUC: 0.7891, p < 0.001) while delivering full post-hoc interpretability via TreeSHAP. papers.title: Belief-integrated timed elastic band planning for robust indoor person following under intermittent observations
papers.abstract: Indoor person-following robots routinely lose sight of their target at corners, doorways, and in crowds, and most local planners then stall at the last seen position. We present IO-TEB (Intermittent-Observation Timed Elastic Band), a local planner that maintains a probabilistic estimate of the hidden person’s position and its growing uncertainty, feeds this estimate directly into trajectory optimization, and actively searches likely paths when the person stays hidden. Across 4,320 simulated episodes covering eight indoor scenes, three occlusion durations, and real pedestrian trajectories, IO-TEB completed 87.36% of following tasks, versus 55.14% for the standard timed elastic band planner. It was statistically equivalent to a conventional design that handles the same estimate in a separate finite-state supervisor, indicating that embedding the estimate in the optimizer costs neither accuracy nor computation. Compared with model predictive control (MPC) using trajectory prediction and three recent person-following planners, IO-TEB was not the most accurate, but in our implementation it missed the 100 ms control-cycle deadline least often (3.32% of cycles versus 5.14–44.21%). Ablation shows that replacing the last observation with the predicted estimate as the following reference accounts for most of the gain, whereas the uncertainty-dependent terms added no consistent benefit.

papers.title: Conceptualizing A Closed-Loop Digital Twin for Real-Time Plasma Control in Large-Area Magnetron Sputtering Systems
papers.abstract: Large-area magnetron sputtering underpins the manufacture of architectural low-emissivity glazing, thin-film photovoltaics, flat-panel and flexible displays, and functional coatings, yet the process remains difficult to control at the fidelity that modern device tolerances demand. The governing plasma is a strongly non-linear, spatially distributed, multi-time-scale system in which small excursions in reactive-gas partial pressure, target erosion state, or magnetic-field topology propagate into large deviations in deposition rate, stoichiometry, and thickness uniformity. Conventional single-input single-output feedback loops built around plasma emission monitoring or optical set-points are effective but cannot reason about the unobserved internal state of the discharge, nor anticipate the slow drifts that dominate long production campaigns. This paper conceptualizes a closed-loop digital twin that fuses reduced-order physics-based and data-driven surrogate models of the discharge with heterogeneous in-situ diagnostics through recursive state estimation, and that closes the loop through predictive and learning-based control. We survey the fundamentals of direct-current, radio-frequency, and high-power impulse magnetron sputtering, the hysteresis and instability phenomena that make reactive processes hard to regulate, and the diagnostic instruments—Langmuir probes, optical emission spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and in-situ metrology—that can supply the twin with real-time observations. Building on the digitaltwin, model-order-reduction, and data-assimilation literatures, we propose a layered architecture spanning the physical asset, a low-latency sensing and data pipeline, coupled twin models, a Kalman-family state estimator, and a control policy realized as model predictive control or reinforcement learning. We define a latency budget across these layers, articulate use cases in uniformity, stoichiometry, arc-suppression, and target-erosion compensation, and set out a validation pathway and research roadmap addressing model fidelity, calibration, uncertainty quantification, verification and validation, and industrial scale-up

papers.title: High-Throughput Polymer Design for the Biological Interface
papers.abstract: Abstract High-throughput experimentation is transforming synthetic polymer design for biological applications, enabling data-driven approaches that map the vast chemical design space accessible to synthetic macromolecules. In this Viewpoint, we survey recent advances in high-throughput methodologies for discovering polymers that interface with biological systems. We first review synthetic strategies, such as well-plate polymerizations, immobilized and solid-phase synthesis, and continuous flow chemistry, that enable parallelized, miniaturized access to large polymer libraries. We then discuss screening methods for structural characterization, target-binding interactions, and functional performance in cellular and biological contexts. We highlight how these readouts capture the disordered, dynamic nature of synthetic polymers relative to structured biomacromolecules. Finally, we examine how machine learning, active learning, self-driving laboratories, and emerging agentic AI tools are being integrated with high-throughput workflows to accelerate inverse design and autonomous experimentation. We underscore the potential of increasingly automated discovery in future years and the need for rigorous, application-appropriate workflow design. Together, these synthesis, characterization, and computational strategies form a synergistic pipeline poised to accelerate the discovery of next-generation polymer therapeutics and biomaterials.

papers.title: Convexity-Preserving Reduced-Complexity Model Predictive Control via Radial Basis Function Networks
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate Model Predictive Control (MPC) for systems operating under state, control, and output constraints, and propose an enhanced formulation that significantly reduces computational demand. Within the MPC framework, we introduce a novel representation of the control signal based on Radial Basis Function Networks (RBFNs)—well known for their strong function approximation capabilities. Instead of optimizing over a conventional vector of discrete control inputs, the proposed approach encodes the control trajectory using a compact set of RBFN weights. This reformulation substantially decreases the number of optimization variables, thereby reducing the computational burden associated with solving constrained quadratic programs in MPC. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the transformation from the standard control space to the RBFN weight space preserves convexity and positive definiteness of the original cost function, ensuring stability and uniqueness of the optimal solution. To evaluate the practical benefits of this approach, the MPC–RBFN method is applied to the longitudinal control of an aircraft model. Simulation results confirm that the proposed controller achieves comparable tracking performance to conventional MPC while providing a marked improvement in computational efficiency, highlighting its suitability for real-time and embedded control applications.

papers.title: The laser powder bed fusion of particle-reinforced aluminum alloy matrix composites
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of aluminum matrix particulate composites (AMPCs) with opportunities for microstructural refinement and precipitation strengthening. However, reported mechanical responses remain highly non-monotonic with respect to particle content. Strength improvements are often accompanied by limited or inconsistent gains in ductility, fatigue performance, and damage tolerance. This review adopts a constraint-first perspective and organizes the literature along a processing-linked constraint pathway. The performance of LPBF-processed AMPCs is interpreted in terms of a hierarchy of coupled physical constraints that become active at different stages. These include processing stability associated with melting behavior, interfacial mechanical and chemical compatibility under rapid thermal cycling, particle redistribution during melt-pool transport and solidification, and the transition of crack initiation control among competing defect populations. Evidence is synthesized across the full processing chain, from energy coupling at the powder bed to melt-pool dynamics, particle redistribution, and defect evolution. This framework helps explain why particle additions lead to improved mechanical performance in some cases, but not in others where processing-induced constraints become dominant. Based on this synthesis, a transferable design framework is proposed. It emphasizes stable processing conditions, interface states that sustain load transfer, control of particle clustering, and performance evaluation based on defect severity rather than average properties. Overall, this review frames LPBF-processed AMPCs as a constraint-governed system, and provides a basis for interpreting scattered results and improving cross-study comparability.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: A Review of Learning Analytics, Personalized Tutoring, Generative AI and Academic Integrity
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now touches most stages of teaching and learning. Learning analytics predicts which students are at risk, knowledge tracing models estimate what each student has mastered, intelligent tutors adapt practice to the learner, and large language models can explain, grade and write. The same tools have created new problems. Generative AI makes it easy to submit text that a student did not write, detection tools are unreliable, and models trained on student data raise questions of privacy and fairness. The problem is that these topics are reviewed in separate literatures: analytics and tutoring surveys rarely discuss academic integrity, and integrity studies rarely discuss the learning models that produce or detect the text. This review brings them into one framework of five layers: learning analytics and prediction, personalization and intelligent tutoring, generative AI in learning, academic integrity, and a cross-cutting layer of privacy, fairness and inclusion. It organizes 42 studies and compares their methods and reported results. Deep knowledge tracing raised the area under the curve from 0.67 to 0.86 over Bayesian knowledge tracing, and intelligent tutoring systems raised test scores by a median of 0.66 standard deviations. A randomized trial found that a carefully designed AI tutor produced learning gains of 0.73 to 1.3 standard deviations over in-class active learning, but a field experiment found that unrestricted GPT-4 access raised practice grades by 48% and then lowered exam grades by 17%. Detection of AI-generated text is weak: tested tools were neither accurate nor reliable, and detectors flagged 61% of essays by non-native English writers as machine-written. Few studies connect personalization with integrity or measure bias across student groups. Future work should design AI tutors with learning safeguards, assess integrity through process rather than detection alone, and evaluate both under privacy protection and across diverse learners.

papers.title: An Intelligent Cyber–Physical Framework for Electric Bus Batteries: Combining DQN Smart Charging with LSTM Digital Twins
papers.abstract: The operational reliability of electric buses depends heavily on the thermal stability and longevity of their battery packs. In urban public transit, highly dynamic driving cycles characterized by severe current surges during regenerative braking and prolonged constantcurrent charging phases induce massive localized thermal stress. Traditional battery management systems often fail to dynamically balance energy recovery with the physical constraints of cell matrices, leading to accelerated degradation and potential safety hazards. This paper proposes an integrated cyber–physical framework that merges intelligent control with advanced prognostic monitoring and predictive thermal management. The core of the control layer is a deep Q-network (DQN) agent designed for real-time smart charging and dynamic regenerative braking current limitation (smart derating). This control loop is tightly integrated with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network-based digital twin (DT) operating at the edge level to mirror complex electro-thermal dynamics and track the battery state of health (SOH). To ensure transparency and proactive thermal control, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy is implemented, utilizing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to map core heat generation and dynamically adjust for internal thermal lag. The predictive NMPC-xAI loop maintained cell temperatures within a tight, optimal envelope, preventing delayed under-cooling and reducing peak temperature fluctuations

papers.title: A conformal virtual metrology framework for predictive uncertainty quantification: a full factorial experimental study of micro crown gear quality
papers.abstract: Abstract Virtual metrology uses process data to estimate product quality before physical measurement results become available. However, most models return only a point prediction, which does not show whether an individual prediction is reliable enough for quality decisions. This paper develops a conformal prediction framework for virtual metrology of micro crown gear quality from acoustic emission signals. The framework combines regression pipelines selected for each quality characteristic with Split conformal prediction (Split CP), cross validation plus (CV+), and cross fitted conformalized quantile regression (CF-CQR). The framework is model agnostic and does not require a parametric form for the distribution of the data. Under exchangeability, conformal prediction provides finite sample marginal coverage guarantees for prediction intervals. Split CP, CV+ and CF-CQR are evaluated over repeated data partitions of the full-factorial experimental dataset using empirical coverage, interval width, and the Winkler score. The results show that acoustic emission signals support the prediction of the studied geometric characteristics, although predictive difficulty varies across targets. The conformal methods provide coverage close to the nominal level, while cross validation plus and cross fitted conformalized quantile regression generally produce more informative intervals than Split conformal prediction. The predicted intervals are used to formulate an interpretable quality assessment logic by distinguishing clear conformity, clear nonconformity, and ambiguous cases that require physical measurement or expert assessment. The proposed framework moves virtual metrology from isolated point predictions towards quality predictions that communicate uncertainty explicitly.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Interactive Digital Learning Media in Increasing High School Students' Learning Motivation
papers.abstract: Digital transformation encourages the use of increasingly interactive learning media, but its effectiveness on student learning motivation is still determined by the pedagogical design and context of use. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of interactive digital learning media in improving learning motivation of high school students. The study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. A total of 120 10th grade students from four high schools in Ambon City, Maluku Province, participated in the study. Schools were selected purposively based on the readiness of digital learning facilities, while classes were selected through cluster sampling; 60 students were in the experimental group and 60 students in the control group. The experimental group participated in Indonesian language learning on the topic of explanatory text using digital media that integrated videos, visual materials, digital quizzes, interactive exercises, and direct feedback for six meetings, while the control group participated in regular learning with the same materials and time allocation. Learning motivation was measured using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and data were analyzed using Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA). The motivation score of the experimental group increased from 3.18 to 4.08, while the control group increased from 3.21 to 3.39. After controlling for baseline scores, there was a significant difference between the two groups, F (1,117) = 79.62, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.405. The largest difference was found in the engagement and interest dimensions. The findings indicate that, in this study sample, interactive digital learning media was associated with higher motivational increases when technology was used to support active learning activities and provide feedback.

papers.title: The GATE Framework: A Generative AI-Enhanced Active Learning Environment for Tourism Communication Competency Development
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being adopted in tourism and hospitality education more quickly than the pedagogical guidance needed to use it well. This study developed the GATE Framework, a GenAI-enhanced active learning environment intended to develop tourism communication competency, and examined its appropriateness through expert review. The work comprised two stages within the first research phase. An evidence-informed synthesis established three connected layers: Inputs, Core Process Components, and Outcomes. At the center of the Process Layer is an iterative Explore-Generate-Apply-Reflect cycle, supported by human-AI interaction, authentic tourism tasks, peer and instructor participation, reflection, and adaptive feedback. In the second stage, nine experts in tourism and hospitality, curriculum and instruction, educational technology, AI in education, and active learning then evaluated the framework using an 18-item, five-point scale and four open-ended questions. The overall rating was very high (x̄ = 4.54, S.D. = 0.58), and the five domain means ranged from 4.52 to 4.56. The experts gave their strongest ratings to the framework's theoretical alignment, relevance to tourism communication learning, and suitability for further development. Ratings remained favorable but were lower for the definition of individual roles and the practical sequence of the learning process. In response, the framework was revised to clarify scaffolding and human oversight, strengthen privacy and transparency provisions, and give greater weight to tourism content rooted in local culture. The resulting framework provides the conceptual basis for GATE-SLE, where GenAI assists disciplinary learning without displacing human judgment.

papers.title: A Statistical Reliability Framework for Markov Epidemic Networks
papers.abstract: Disease progression can be statistically represented as a network of patient states connected by transition probabilities, providing a natural basis for quantifying progression toward favorable and unfavorable outcomes. This study develops a statistical reliability framework for disease progression networks based on discrete-time Markov transitions, integrating maximum-likelihood estimation, first-passage reliability, bootstrap uncertainty quantification, and probability-simplex-constrained sensitivity analysis. The framework converts patient-level longitudinal trajectories into an estimated transition structure and subsequently quantifies the probability of reaching a favorable target state before an absorbing unfavorable outcome. A row-preserving perturbation strategy is used to assess the influence of individual transitions while maintaining the probability constraints, and a dimensionless elasticity measure is introduced to rank transitions according to their contribution to network reliability. Monte Carlo experiments demonstrate stable statistical performance of the proposed estimator: for the specified baseline network, the true reliability is approximately 0.7483, while the RMSE decreases from 0.0465 for n=100 to 0.0098 for n=2000, indicating substantial improvement in estimation accuracy as the sample size increases. The sensitivity analysis further identifies the most influential transitions, with progression from localized disease to treatment and treatment to remission showing the strongest positive effects on reliability, whereas transitions toward death exhibit negative effects. The framework is also applied to a real longitudinal breast cancer dataset comprising 169 patient records. The empirical analysis identifies 16 recurrence events and four deaths and characterizes the observed treatment, surgery, recurrence, and survival-time patterns. Importantly, because the available clinical variables do not unambiguously identify all states of the theoretical seven-state model, the real-data analysis is restricted to directly observable patient events rather than imposing unsupported clinical state assignments. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a statistically interpretable pipeline linking patient-level transition data, network reliability, uncertainty quantification, and transition importance, with potential applications to reliability-based analysis of multistate disease progression and other longitudinal health processes.

papers.title: A Bibliometric and Network Analysis of Statistical Distributions in Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Statistical distributions constitute a fundamental component of machine learning by providing the probabilistic framework required for modelling uncertainty, variability, and data-generating processes. They underpin a wide range of methodologies, including Bayesian inference, probabilistic graphical models, generative learning and uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence. Despite their widespread application, the evolution and intellectual structure of research on statistical distributions in machine learning have not been systematically examined. This study presents a bibliometric and network analysis of 840 Scopus-indexed publications published between 1997 and 2025. Bibliographic data were analysed using Biblioshiny and VOS viewer to evaluate publication trends, influential sources, author productivity, collaboration patterns and thematic developments. Descriptive indicators were complemented by co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and thematic analyses to explore the social and intellectual structure of the field. The findings reveal sustained growth in research output, increasing international collaboration and the dominance of a core set of journals and authors. Network analyses identify probabilistic modelling, Bayesian learning, uncertainty quantification and generative approaches as the principal intellectual foundations of the field. The results further indicate a gradual shift from classical statistical learning frameworks toward uncertainty-aware and explainable machine learning paradigms. By mapping the evolution, knowledge structure and emerging directions of this research domain, the study provides a comprehensive reference for future investigations at the intersection of statistical distribution theory and machine learning.

papers.title: Prognostic maintenance and smart monitoring of solar panel using IoT devices and hybrid machine learning models
papers.abstract: The profusion, flexibility, and recurrently declining installation costs of solar photovoltaic (PV) technology have made it a protuberant renewable energy source. However, environmental unpredictability, component deterioration, power-electronic failures, and aging effects continue to have a major impact on the long-term performance and reliability of PV systems. There are some drawbacks to the conventional maintenance techniques employed in PV installations, such as routine manual inspections and corrective actions. In order to improve the performance and operational efficiency of solar PV systems, this work presents a prognostic maintenance framework driven by machine learning techniques and enabled by IoT device. A low cost hardware prototype of real time solar data acquisition and monitoring system is developed using LoRa module which collects data from the solar station and in the transmitter station the data is pushed to cloud and displayed in dashboard. Different machine learning models linear regression, decision tree, random forest and XGBoost has been implemented for predictive maintenance of solar panels. A hybrid machine learning model based on Bayesian optimization of XGBoost is proposed and from the comparative assessment of the machine learning models it is validated that the proposed hybrid model showed superior performance in terms of highest accuracy and lowest computation time.

papers.title: Potential of the Discovery Learning Model with a Cognitive Conflict Approach on Students’ Problem-Solving Skills: A Review
papers.abstract: Problem-solving skills are one of the key 21st-century competencies that can be developed through active learning. Although various studies have demonstrated the positive impact of the discovery learning model on problem-solving skills, research that integrates current trends with a synthesis of findings regarding the role of learning approaches- particularly the cognitive conflict approach-remains limited. This study aims to analyze trends in research on the discovery learning model as it relates to students’ problem-solving skills and to examine trends in the integration of learning approaches that support its implementation. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PRISMA framework combined with bibliometric analysis. Bibliometric data were obtained from the Scopus database and analyzed using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. Meanwhile, thematic analysis was conducted on 22 selected articles from Google Scholar and Scopus. Bibliometric findings suggest that research on discovery learning and problem-solving skills remains an active area of study, particularly in science and chemistry education. Recent research has explored the use of discovery learning alongside various approaches and strategies to promote active learning. Thematic synthesis further shows that discovery learning has generally been found to be effective in improving students' problem-solving skills. It can also be improved by using the right media, learning strategies, and teaching methods. The cognitive conflict method of learning, among others, has been highlighted in the literature as a learning approach that fits here, since it enables the restructuring of concepts.

papers.abstract: The school-based oral health promoting program was developed to build oral health literacy among upper primary school students with health teachers delivering the program alongside a digital platform through active learning. This activity format has a single nationwide standard, with health teachers serving as the main party responsible for its implementation in each school. This qualitative study aimed to analyze the inequality in the adaptation burden faced by health teachers in carrying out this activity, under varying levels of resource readiness across different school contexts covering readiness, obstacles, support networks, and the approaches health teachers propose for the program's sustainability. Data were collected using purposive sampling with maximum variation, drawn from 6 primary schools across 4 regions with differing levels of cooperation and resource readiness. The main informants were 14 health teachers, supplemented by data from 7 school administrators to provide context on the management environment. In-depth interviews adapted from the CIPP Model framework were used, with data analyzed through thematic analysis and credibility verified through triangulation until data saturation was reached. The findings showed that the health teachers' adaptation burden was concentrated among health teachers in small schools and rural areas with more limited resources. papers.title: Hybrid Biofabrication of a Hierarchically Organized Periosteum-Inspired In Vitro Platform.
papers.abstract: The periosteum is a hierarchically organized, vascularized membrane essential for skeletal maintenance and regeneration, yet in vitro models that reproduce its compartmentalized and multicellular architecture remain limited. In this study, we present a hierarchically organized, periosteum-inspired in vitro platform fabricated by integrating melt electrowriting (MEW) with extrusion-based 3D bioprinting. The platform integrates a human osteoblast-laden plasma-containing alginate/methylcellulose hydrogel compartment, a configurable MEW-PCL microfibrous interface, and an endothelial cell-fibroblast-laden fibrin/gelatin hydrogel compartment. MEW scaffold architectures and compartment-specific bioink-cell configurations were screened based on their ability to support osteogenic maturation-associated readouts and CD31+ endothelial cell organization. The resulting tri-layer construct maintained high cytocompatibility and structural integrity during culture for up to 49 days. The osteogenic compartment supported osteogenic differentiation-associated readouts and mineralized matrix deposition, while the endothelial cell-containing compartment supported interconnected CD31+ endothelial cell organization accompanied by endothelial cell-associated gene expression. Overall, this hybrid MEW-3D bioprinted platform provides an engineerable in vitro model for periosteum-inspired tissue modeling, biomaterial screening, and investigation of osteogenic and endothelial cell-associated processes under controlled conditions.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postmenopausal osteoporosis associated with cafeteria diet and bisphosphonate therapy may impair peri-implant bone repair. Therefore, strategies to enhance osseointegration are needed. AIM: This study investigated whether teriparatide-coated implant surfaces enhance osseointegration in a rodent model of estrogen deficiency (OVX) and cafeteria diet (CD) treated with risedronate (RIS). MATERIAL AND METHODS: In the in vitro phase, titanium discs coated with 10 or 40 ng of teriparatide were evaluated by in vitro bioassays, and drug adsorption was confirmed by UV-Vis spectroscopy. As both loading amounts produced similar biological responses, 10 ng was selected for the in vivo phase. In the in vivo phase, 48 rats were randomly assigned to SHAM (sham-operated control), OVX/CD (ovariectomized with cafeteria diet), or OVX/CD/RIS (ovariectomized with cafeteria diet and risedronate) groups. Titanium implants either coated with teriparatide using a layer-by-layer topical drug delivery system or left non-coated were placed bilaterally in the maxilla. Rats were euthanized after 28 days. Osseointegration was evaluated by removal torque testing, micro computed tomography, fluorescence microscopy, and RT-qPCR analysis. RESULTS: In the cell culture experiment, both teriparatide amounts successfully promoted mineralized nodule formation in vitro and UV-Vis spectroscopy confirmed drug adsorption. In vivo, teriparatide significantly increased removal torque across all groups, with the greatest increase in OVX/CD/RIS. Teriparatide also increased peri-implant bone volume in OVX/CD and OVX/CD/RIS, confirmed by micro computed tomography and fluorescence microscopy. RT-qPCR also confirmed upregulation of osteogenic and angiogenic markers. CONCLUSION: Topical teriparatide delivery improves peri-implant bone repair under estrogen deficiency, cafeteria diet, and bisphosphonate therapy.

papers.abstract: Anticipating short-term hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic risk is essential for proactive diabetes management. However, existing machine learning approaches often use inconsistent evaluation protocols and emphasize predictive performance over reliability. This study introduces an anchor-based benchmarking framework integrating longitudinal glucose sequences and multimodal patient information. Using the T1DiabetesGranada dataset, 5,503,441 standardized prediction anchors were constructed from 736 individuals with type 1 diabetes to evaluate hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia prediction at 30-, 60-, and 120-minute horizons. Three neural architectures, a Hybrid LSTM-Transformer, a Multimodal Digital Twin, and a State-Updating Digital Twin with gap-aware longitudinal state progression, were compared under identical patient-level validation protocols. Beyond predictive performance, the evaluation examined calibration, classification thresholds, explanation reliability, cross-model disagreement, and robustness to controlled perturbations. No statistically significant predictive differences were observed after Holm correction, although the models exhibited complementary reliability characteristics. The Multimodal Digital Twin achieved the lowest mean Brier score, while the State-Updating Digital Twin demonstrated the lowest mean expected calibration error (ECE-10). The Hybrid LSTM-Transformer showed strong explanation faithfulness and stability under its temporal attribution protocol. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating digital-twin models beyond predictive accuracy and emphasize the need for reliability assessment and external validation before clinical deployment.

papers.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.

papers.title: Efficient regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation models
papers.abstract: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.

papers.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.

papers.title: A Graph-informed Kriging model for sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts
papers.abstract: Wind farm layout optimization becomes increasingly difficult as turbine count grows, especially when high-fidelity aerodynamic models are used. Conventional Kriging-based Bayesian optimization often suffers from low sample efficiency in high-dimensional layout spaces because sparse training data provide limited domain coverage. We develop a Graph-informed Kriging framework that embeds reusable aerodynamic interaction information into the surrogate mean function. The wind farm is represented as a directed aerodynamic graph, where pairwise turbine interactions defined in a low-dimensional relative-coordinate space are assembled into a farm-scale mean. This structured mean captures the dominant variation in annual energy production (AEP), allowing the Gaussian process to model only the residual structure and uncertainty. Numerical experiments show that Graph-informed Kriging consistently improves AEP prediction accuracy over ordinary and generic-trend Kriging under sparse-data conditions, with increasing benefits as layout dimension and wake-interaction strength grow. Embedded in Bayesian optimization, it substantially improves sample efficiency and achieves competitive solutions for the IEA Wind Task 37 benchmark with about 280 AEP evaluations. In a controlled 16-turbine case, it also outperforms ordinary and multi-fidelity Kriging under the same high-fidelity evaluation budget. The framework is further extended to a 48-turbine wind farm, demonstrating applicability to large-scale CFD-based layout optimization. These results show that Graph-informed surrogate modeling can enable more efficient use of high-fidelity aerodynamic models for reliable large-scale wind farm layout design.

papers.title: TREATMENT AND PROSTHETIC REHABILITATION USING SINGLE AND MULTIPLE IMPLANTS IN ATROPHIC JAWS IN CANCER PATIENTS
papers.abstract: Oncological treatment in the head and neck region often requires extensive resective surgeries, resulting in severe bone and functional deficiencies in the jaws. Prosthetic rehabilitation with single and multiple implants in atrophic jaws emerges as a fundamental alternative for restoring mastication, phonation, and aesthetics in oncological patients. This study consists of a narrative literature review aimed at synthesizing contemporary surgical and prosthetic approaches in this scenario. Reconstruction with microvascularized free flaps (fibula and iliac crest – DCIA), combined with 3D virtual surgical planning, provides high precision in bone repositioning and implant anchorage. Radiotherapy acts as a critical factor in osseointegration, with higher success rates when implants are placed before radiotherapy or after prolonged latency intervals. Screw-retained fixed prostheses on machined abutments are the preferred choice because they reduce trauma to fragile mucosa. It is concluded that the predictability of rehabilitative treatment depends on multidisciplinary planning, combining surgical precision, rigorous biofilm control, and continuous histopathological monitoring of peri-implant tissues.

papers.title: Advances in 3D Bioprinting for Dental, Oral, and Craniofacial Regenerative Medicine
papers.abstract: Regeneration of the dental, oral, and craniofacial (DOC) complex is challenging because mineralized, soft, vascular, and neural tissues lie side by side, and defects are often large and irregular. Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting enables fabrication of patient-specific, cell-laden constructs and may offer new regenerative options for complex oral cases. This narrative review summarizes current bioprinting technologies, their applications across DOC tissues, and the barriers to clinical adoption. Inkjet, laser-assisted, light-based, extrusion, and co-axial platforms differ in speed, resolution, cell viability, and cost, while intraoperative bioprinting allows constructs to be printed directly into the defect during surgery. Hydrogel-based bioinks, often loaded with cells or growth factors, support cell delivery and guided differentiation. Across the dentin–pulp complex, periodontium, gingiva, salivary glands, peripheral nerves, cartilage, and craniofacial bone, preclinical studies report that bioprinted constructs can recreate tissue microarchitecture, enhance vascularization, and support partial functional repair. Whole-tooth and load-bearing bone regeneration remain constrained by spatial patterning, vascularization, and mechanical demands. Most evidence remains preclinical, and translation is limited by cost, fragmented workflows, biological and mechanical mismatch at tissue interfaces, and unclear regulatory pathways. Standardized fidelity and viability metrics, improved bioinks, and point-of-care workflows will be needed before bioprinting becomes part of routine oral regenerative care.

papers.abstract: Aluminum alloys with high strength-to-weight ratios are attractive for demanding aerospace and automotive applications. However, processing high-strength alloys, particularly 2xxx, 6xxx, and 7xxx series, by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) remains challenging due to their high cracking susceptibility. To overcome these limitations, aluminum metal matrix composites (AMMCs) have emerged as a promising alternative. This study investigates the processability of Al2024-RAM2, containing Ti and B4C particles as inoculants that promote in situ reactions during processing. The effect of reaction extent, influenced by different processing parameter combinations and heat treatment, was analyzed in relation to the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties. EBSD mapping revealed a fully fine equiaxed microstructure, attributed to a columnar-to-equiaxed transition (CET) during solidification promoted by the reinforcing particles, which increase the density of nucleation sites. Under optimized processing conditions and heat treatment, relative densities of up to ~99.9% were achieved. The resulting material exhibited a hardness of 160 HV, tensile strength exceeding 480 MPa, and elongation close to 10%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the reinforcement strategy in improving the PBF-LB/M processability of a high-strength Al2024-based alloy while achieving a favorable combination of strength and ductility.

papers.abstract: Abstract The distal tibiofibular syndesmosis injuries are a common type of ankle injury. Traditional rigid screw fixation presents issues such as restricting physiological micromotion and requiring a second surgery for removal. The existing elastic fixation techniques have limitations, including insufficient fixation strength and nonadjustable tension. This technical note describes an arthroscopic‐assisted adjustable progressive compression fixation technique. By rotating the fibular‐side EndoButton, the 4‐strand high‐tensile sutures synchronously twist and shorten, achieving continuous and controllable transverse compression of the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis. This technique combines the strength of rigid fixation with the physiological compliance of elastic fixation. Intraoperatively, tension can be adjusted in real‐time based on tactile feedback, direct arthroscopic visualization, and fluoroscopic imaging, achieving an optimal balance between stability and micromotion. This technique provides a reliable fixation option for distal tibiofibular syndesmosis injuries.

papers.title: Can AI be Easy? Lessons Learned From the EZR.py Toolkit
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Much recent press claims that developers no longer need to read code. We disagree, at least within the domain of tabular software‐engineering (SE) optimization tasks: rows of and values where the values are expensive to obtain. As evidence, we present EZR.py, a Python toolkit of less than 1000 lines (no heavy dependencies) that implements Naive Bayes, ‐means clustering, classification and regression trees, simulated annealing, local search, active learning, and complementary‐Bayes text‐mining relevance filtering for tabular SE data. EZR was built by repeatedly reading and refactoring AI tools to simplify and unify them. The result demonstrates that many seemingly different learning algorithms are nearly the same once stripped back to their core: classical algorithms collapse to a few lines each, and a state‐of‐the‐art active learner fits in roughly 80 lines. This paper shows that (a) on 20 randomly selected benchmarks from the MOOT repository of 124 tabular SE optimization tasks, simulated annealing in its 1983 default configuration matches or beats more elaborate local‐search variants; (b) an 80‐line active learner reaches 85%–95% of the reference optimum with fewer than 100 labels across the MOOT tasks , building trees from fewer than ten variables even when thousands are available; and (c) on Yu et al.'s four systematic‐review corpora, a 30‐line complementary‐Bayes filter matches the recall of the SVM‐based FASTREAD text miner using roughly one‐third of the labels , on three of the four corpora; on the fourth, it converges faster but plateaus below FASTREAD's recall ceiling (a tradeoff detailed in §7) . Companion studies (coauthored by authors of this paper) further report that this active learner's model update runs over 400 times faster than SMAC3, and that its trees rank features as well as SHAP and ReliefF. We conclude that, within the scope of tabular SE optimization, reading and refactoring code is a useful method of generating insight, and small unified toolkits can rival large libraries. EZR is available under an open‐source license. Install via pip install ezr (Python 3.12). The exact version studied here (release v0.9.4 ) is archived at Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22554751 ; example data at github.com/timm/moot . See Appendix A for notes on installing and running this code.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Advanced Materials Modeling in Thermal, Energy, and Aerodynamic Systems: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming the development and analysis of advanced materials and engineering systems by enabling data-driven prediction, materials discovery, simulation acceleration, and optimization. However, the rapidly expanding literature remains fragmented across materials science, thermofluid modeling, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), physics-informed learning, reduced-order modeling, and digital twins. This study presents a systematic review of AI applications in advanced materials, thermal and energy systems, and aerodynamic engineering using a PRISMA-based methodology. A systematic search was conducted in the Scopus database for peer-reviewed studies published between 2019 and 2026. From 1468 records initially identified through Scopus, 122 studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included from the database-search pathway, while six additional studies identified through other methods were assessed separately against the substantive eligibility requirements and retained, resulting in a final corpus of 128 studies that were subsequently subjected to methodological quality assessment. The review identifies major applications of Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), generative AI, and materials informatics in materials property prediction, characterization, screening, and design. It further examines AI-assisted CFD and thermofluid modeling, including heat and mass transfer, turbulence modeling, flow prediction, and aerodynamic optimization. The analysis also highlights the growing role of physics-informed learning, reduced-order and surrogate models, optimization algorithms, and digital twins in improving computational efficiency and supporting intelligent engineering decision-making. Despite these advances, data availability, generalization, uncertainty quantification, validation, computational cost, scalability, and interoperability remain important barriers to practical implementation. Overall, the literature indicates a transition from isolated AI-based prediction toward integrated physics–data-driven engineering frameworks that connect materials development, simulation, optimization, and real-time system operation.

papers.title: Clinical evidence on nonantibiotic antibacterial strategies for reducing the risk of periprosthetic joint infection: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most devastating complications in orthopedic surgery, associated with substantial morbidity, high treatment costs, and increased mortality. Although antibiotic therapy remains the cornerstone of prevention and treatment, the emergence of antimicrobial resistance has driven the development of alternative antibacterial strategies targeting implant surfaces and the local biological environment. However, the clinical effectiveness of these nonantibiotic approaches has not yet been fully established. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify nonantibiotic antibacterial strategies currently applied in clinical practice, to evaluate their effectiveness in preventing or managing PJI and to quantify, through meta-analysis, the comparative infection-prevention effect of silver-coated versus uncoated prostheses. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. The search was performed on 27 January 2026 and included studies published over the last 10 years (January 2015–December 2025). Eligible studies comprised clinical investigations assessing nonantibiotic antibacterial strategies in patients undergoing primary or revision orthopedic procedures. Interventions included antibacterial implant coatings, physicochemical surface modifications, and biologically based antimicrobial therapies. Primary outcomes were infection prevention/control, and reinfection; secondary outcomes included implant survival, adverse events, and function. Risk-of-bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk-of-Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Studies with extractable raw infection counts for silver-coated versus uncoated prostheses were pooled in a random-effects meta-analysis to estimate absolute risk reduction (ARR) and number needed to treat (NNT). Twenty-nine studies, including 2100 patients, met the inclusion criteria. Silver-coated prostheses were the most studied strategy, showing a trend toward reduced infection and improved limb salvage, not always significant. Ten comparative studies (1207 patients: 546 silver-coated, 661 uncoated) were meta-analyzed: pooled infection rates were 12.3% versus 14.5%, yielding an ARR of 3.95% (95% CI −1.02 to 8.91%) favoring silver coating (not significant), NNT ≈ 25. Heterogeneity was moderate ( I 2 = 23.2%). Silver-hydroxyapatite-coated total hip arthroplasty (THA) showed excellent infection prevention without loosening or toxicity. Iodine-coated implants had the strongest evidence, significantly reducing deep infection versus uncoated implants. Bacteriophage therapy was promising but limited to small case series or case reports. Other approaches, particularly based on bacteriophage therapy, showed promising results but were mainly supported by small case series or case reports. Overall, the evidence was limited by a moderate-to-critical risk-of-bias due to nonrandomized study designs and confounding by indication. Nonantibiotic antibacterial strategies, particularly implant coatings, represent promising adjuncts for reducing infection risk in high-risk orthopedic procedures, supported by a growing body of comparative clinical evidence. Bacteriophage therapy, by contrast, remains experimental, currently supported only by case reports and small case series and should not yet be regarded as an adjunct applied in routine clinical practice. Overall, current clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Well-designed prospective controlled studies are needed to clarify the effectiveness of these strategies and to define their role within contemporary infection-prevention protocols.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion', before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

papers.title: Optimizing flow distribution and heat transfer in enhanced geothermal systems: Advances, challenges, and outlook
papers.abstract: Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) offer a scalable pathway for baseload renewable energy, yet their long-term performance is strongly constrained by flow channeling, thermal short-circuiting, and the complex coupling between fracture networks, fluid transport, and heat transfer. This review provides a critical synthesis of recent analytical and numerical studies on fluid flow and heat transfer in fractured geothermal reservoirs, with emphasis on flow partitioning in fracture networks, thermal breakthrough behavior, working fluid selection, and operational controls. The evolution of modeling approaches is summarized, from early analytical and semi-analytical formulations to high-resolution, fracture-resolved numerical frameworks. Key findings consistently show that fracture geometry, connectivity, orientation, and permeability govern reservoir sweep efficiency and the sustainability of heat extraction, while injection strategy strongly influences the onset of thermal decline. Comparative assessments of water and supercritical CO 2 as working fluids indicate that CO 2 can enhance heat extraction and pressure management under regulated operating conditions, although performance remains highly sensitive to fracture-scale transport properties and reservoir heterogeneity. Despite significant progress, most existing models neglect fully coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical–chemical processes, fracture evolution, multiphase flow, and long-term permeability degradation, limiting predictive reliability for multi-decade operation. The review identifies critical research gaps and outlines priorities for next-generation EGS modeling, including fully coupled, field-calibrated frameworks with uncertainty quantification, to support reliable reservoir design and long-term performance assessment.

papers.title: Digital transformation in nursing education: students’ satisfaction, academic self-efficacy, and challenges with interactive e-books
papers.abstract: With the increasing integration of digital tools in nursing education, interactive e-books have emerged as innovative resources that promote engagement, flexibility, and active learning. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness in enhancing nursing students’ satisfaction and academic self-efficacy, as well as the challenges affecting their use, remains limited. This study aimed to assess nursing students’ satisfaction, academic self-efficacy, and perceived challenges related to the use of interactive e-books. A mixed-methods design was employed among 500 undergraduate nursing students at Capital University, Egypt. Quantitative data were collected using validated instruments measuring satisfaction and academic self-efficacy. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were used to examine relationships between variables, while multiple linear regression analysis was conducted to identify key predictors of both outcomes. In addition, qualitative data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires and analyzed thematically to explore students’ perceived challenges related to the use of interactive e-books. The majority of students reported high levels of satisfaction (72.2%) and self-efficacy (63%). A strong positive association was observed between satisfaction and self-efficacy. Multiple linear regression analysis identified academic performance (GPA) as a significant predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.185, p < 0.001) and self-efficacy (β = 0.198, p < 0.001). Prior training was also a significant predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.142, p = 0.014) and self-efficacy (β = 0.155, p = 0.005). Age and academic level were additionally significant predictors across both models, whereas gender was not statistically significant ( p > 0.05). The regression models explained a moderate proportion of variance in both outcomes, emphasizing the multifactorial nature of satisfaction and self-efficacy in technology-enhanced learning environments. Qualitative findings revealed key barriers, including technical limitations, content navigation difficulties, limited access to devices and internet connectivity, cognitive overload, and insufficient digital literacy. Interactive e-books can enhance nursing students’ satisfaction and self-efficacy; however, their effectiveness depends on students’ academic preparedness, technological accessibility, and system design. Addressing identified barriers and strengthening digital readiness are essential for optimizing the integration of interactive e-books in nursing education. Not applicable.

Experiments on 47.82 million anonymized bidding records improve CTR by 23.7%, CVR by 31.2%, ROI by 23.5% over DQN and increase ROI by 6.1% over GAVE and 8.6% over DiffBid. A 2 × 2 factorial ablation confirms significant generator‐agent interaction ( = 0.37 ROI units, 95% CI [0.24, 0.51], = 0.008, = 0.024). Cross‐dataset transfer on iPinYou preserves rankings with 7.0% ROI advantage over GAVE; counterfactual OPE on real logs (SNIPS, doubly robust, auction replay) agrees with simulator ranking. The system achieves 87.4% sample utilization (distinct from GPU utilization 92.30%) and 14.8 ms mean inference latency (p50/p95/p99 = 12.4/18.7/23.1 ms; 100% SLA at 100,000 req/s). papers.title: Research Status and Prospect of Machine Learning in Material Performance Prediction: A Case Study of Conventional and Solid Waste Concrete
papers.abstract: Accelerated global urbanization places multiple pressures on the cement concrete industry, including resource consumption, carbon emissions, and solid waste disposal. Converting solid waste into construction materials offers a viable path towards its large-scale, high-value utilization, driving the green, low-carbon transition of the construction sector. However, solid waste concrete exhibits high-dimensional, multivariable, and strongly nonlinear characteristics owing to coupled factors such as waste type, source, substitution rate, mix proportions, and curing conditions. Consequently, traditional empirical methods fail to meet engineering needs, particularly in efficient mix design, performance prediction, and quality control. In conventional concrete research, predictive modeling has evolved from classical algorithms to ensemble and deep learning frameworks, often optimized via Bayesian optimization or genetic algorithms. Post-hoc interpretability methods such as SHAP and PDP are widely applied to accurately predict compressive strength, identify critical factors, reveal micro-mechanisms, and reconstruct empirical equations. In contrast, research on solid waste concrete has focused heavily on data challenges stemming from varied waste sources, including data heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and noise. In this field, swarm intelligence algorithms (such as particle swarm, grey wolf, and firefly algorithms) are commonly combined with ensemble models to improve prediction accuracy and engineering usability. However, limitations remain in data availability, feature consistency, cross-material transferability, and practical engineering application. Future research should leverage transfer learning, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), and in-situ monitoring to advance models from standalone prediction tools into transferable, interpretable decision-support systems.

papers.title: Delay-Aware Risk-Adaptive Model Predictive Control for Delivery Robot Navigation in Pedestrian Corridors
papers.abstract: Last-mile delivery robots frequently navigate pedestrian-rich local corridors, where sensing, tracking, communication, and computation delays can make pedestrian observations stale and degrade collision-risk estimation. This paper develops a delay-aware risk-adaptive model predictive control (MPC) pipeline that coordinates observation-age compensation and continuous multi-parameter adaptation in a common candidate-based planner. A normalized interaction-risk score jointly schedules the reference speed, pedestrian-avoidance weight, and motion-smoothness weight, enabling efficient motion in low-risk situations and progressively more conservative behavior as predicted risk increases. The method is evaluated through 800 performance simulations, including a 480-run main study over three pedestrian densities, four observation delays, and ten random seeds, a 240-run ablation study, and an 80-run 40 m extended-route evaluation. In the main study, the proposed method achieves a 100% goal-reaching rate, compared with 81.7% for the efficiency-oriented baseline, while reducing average collision count and collision duration by 61.5% and 74.8%, respectively, and increasing minimum robot–human distance by 55.9%. The corresponding collision-free run rate reaches 69.2%. Among successful runs, its mean completion time is 15.32 s, only 6.9% longer than the efficiency-oriented baseline. At a 1.0 s observation delay, the proposed method reduces collision count by 70.2% relative to the efficiency-oriented controller and by 49.9% relative to rule-based switching, while reducing absolute clearance-estimation error to 0.056 m under the tested prescribed pedestrian-motion model. Ablation results confirm that both delay compensation and adaptive weighting contribute to the improvement. On the 40 m extended route, the proposed controller retains a 100% goal-reaching rate and a 70% collision-free run rate. Its mean decision time and average run-wise 95th-percentile decision time are 58.28 ms and 74.21 ms, respectively, both below the 100 ms control period, indicating real-time potential without a measurable average computational penalty.

papers.title: Stagnation-Point Casson Fluid Flow with Variable Properties and Heat Flux: An Adaptive PINN Approach
papers.abstract: The objective of this research is to explore the nature of non-linear flow and heat transfer of the Casson fluid at the stagnation region in view of variable surface heat flux, viscous dissipation, and temperature-dependent thermal properties of the fluid. The model developed here represents the influence of non-linear rheological behavior, surface thermal loading, viscous heating, and variations in fluid properties on flow dynamics. The nonlinear boundary layer equations are reduced to a dimensionless form and solved using the Residual-Based Adaptive Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network (RAP-PINN) method. This is an improvement on traditional numerical solution methods, which repeatedly solve each parameter combination separately. The new approach incorporates the physics into the training algorithm and places more importance on regions where there are higher residual errors. This allows the network to learn the physics-based solution for different governing parameters while keeping the accuracy of the solution high. An investigation of the influence of velocity ratio parameter, Casson parameter, Eckert number, and variable property parameters on the velocity, nanoparticle concentration, and temperature profiles along with their respective heat and mass transfer behaviors is conducted. Comparison with already published results shows very good consistency, which once again verifies the efficiency, accuracy, and reliability of the presented RAP-PINN approach in solving the present nonlinear problem. The suggested model can be used especially in the fields of thermal management, coating and polymer processing, cooling processes, and other engineering applications that involve non-Newtonian fluids under non-uniform thermal boundary conditions.

papers.abstract: Background: Malaria continues to pose a significant global public health challenge, as reflected in the estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 associated deaths recorded worldwide in 2024. Elimination efforts are threatened by antimalarial drug resistance, relapsing Plasmodium vivax infections, and emerging zoonotic Plasmodium knowlesi. Accurate species-level identification is critical for appropriate treatment and surveillance, yet conventional microscopy is labor-intensive and operator-dependent, while rapid diagnostic tests lack sensitivity and species-discrimination capacity. This diagnostic gap underscores the need for automated, trustworthy AI-based tools. papers.title: Exact Multi-Source Evaluation for National-Scale EV Charging Station Placement: How Far Does Surrogate Assistance Take Us?
papers.abstract: Selecting facility locations on a national road network requires evaluating, for every candidate configuration, the shortest-path distance from each demand node to its nearest facility. We show that this objective admits a single multi-source shortest-path sweep rather than K independent single-source Dijkstra searches, which reduces the cost of one exact evaluation on the Great Britain network (12.8 million nodes, 5.4 million demand points) from an estimated 158 s to about 1 s and makes a fully exact national-scale baseline computationally tractable. We build this exact evaluator and use it as a benchmark for surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization. We propose GP-SA-MOEA, a Gaussian process surrogate-assisted multi-objective evolutionary algorithm that replaces most expensive distance evaluations with a learned surrogate while correcting it through uncertainty-guided active learning. On a London benchmark with a computable exactly evaluated reference front, GP-SA-MOEA recovers a diverse front (hypervolume ratio 0.995), whereas a pure surrogate without active learning spuriously dominates the reference front by underestimating distances. At national scale, an exactly evaluated NSGA-II baseline built on this evaluator attains a better Pareto front than GP-SA-MOEA at lower cost (mean IGD 556 vs. 4378, in 1.3 h vs. 5.9 h), and the Euclidean proxy is the closer of the two surrogates in aggregate mean. We therefore ask when surrogate assistance is still worthwhile, and answer with a topology-sensitive benchmark: geometric (Euclidean) assignment fails systematically where water barriers and one-way restrictions make network distance diverge from straight-line distance, selecting the wrong facility for every cross-water demand node on both network versions. These findings position the multi-source exact evaluator as a practical route to large-scale multi-objective facility location and delimit the role of surrogate assistance in this setting.

The model was trained using the Adam optimiser and binary cross-entropy loss across four training configurations of 100, 120, 140, and 180 epochs. papers.title: Multivariate Seismic Fragility Analysis of Curved Rocking Bridges Using Active Learning‐Enhanced Surrogate Modeling
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Curved bridges with rocking piers offer enhanced seismic resilience but introduce complex interactions among horizontal curvature, bidirectional ground motion, and nonlinear rocking mechanisms, making traditional univariate fragility models insufficient. To address these challenges, the proposed method integrates active learning with Natural Gradient Boosting (AL‐NGB) to construct data‐efficient surrogate models for seismic demand estimation under high‐dimensional uncertainty. A comprehensive dataset comprising 2000 curved rocking bridge models and scaled ground motions is developed to train and validate the surrogate framework. Feature selection via feature importance and correlation analysis identifies S d ,T1 and FI as dominant intensity measures for predicting the average responses of the pier, bearing, shear key, and abutment, which are adopted as the engineering demand parameters. The AL‐NGB framework achieves comparable accuracy to full‐data models using only 10% of the training samples, significantly reducing computational cost. Fragility analyses reveal that system‐level seismic vulnerability of curved rocking bridges is strongly governed by critical components (e.g., shear keys) and is highly sensitive to the directionality of seismic excitation highlighting the need for direction‐aware design. This study demonstrates the potential of combining active learning with probabilistic machine learning for data‐efficient and high‐fidelity seismic risk assessment of complex bridge systems.

papers.title: Predicting Early Unplanned Readmission to Critical Care Units Using Machine Learning and Metaheuristic Hyperparameter Optimization: Evidence from a Chilean Public Hospital
papers.abstract: Background: Early unplanned readmission to critical care units is associated with adverse outcomes and consumes scarce capacity twice, yet the decision to transfer a patient out of the unit is still made without objective criteria. Machine learning may support this decision, but metaheuristic hyperparameter search remains largely unexplored here. Methods: We analyzed 371 patients discharged from the critical care unit of a Chilean public hospital, of whom 41 were readmitted within seven days of transfer to a general ward. Five models (logistic regression, support vector classification, decision tree, random forest, and XGBoost) were trained on clinical and nursing variables available at transfer, using nested stratified five-fold cross-validation with preprocessing fitted within the training folds. Bayesian optimization and a genetic algorithm were compared under identical folds. Results: Under nested cross-validation, discrimination was moderate (AUC 53.3–75.2%), and no single model performed best across all metrics. Logistic regression achieved the highest AUC (75.2%) with the lowest variability across folds, followed by XGBoost (75.0%), whose results varied markedly across folds. The genetic algorithm yielded higher AUC than Bayesian optimization for most tree-based models. Days in the critical care unit, age, and unit of origin ranked highest in impurity-based importance. Conclusions: This proof-of-concept study suggests that routinely collected clinical and nursing information available at transfer may inform early readmission prediction. As the sample was case-enriched and derived from a single center, recalibration to the natural readmission prevalence and prospective external validation are required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Event-triggered communication reduces unnecessary transmissions in unmanned surface vehicle (USV) formations, but leaves two connected trajectory-level problems. Between leader state packets, the follower side must maintain a leader trajectory prediction; after a new packet arrives, the current and updated reference trajectories may not connect. We propose an event-domain prediction–adaptation–replanning framework to address both problems. Under ideal-link conditions, the leader- and follower-side synchronized event-domain state–residual physics-informed neural network (PINN) trajectory predictors generate identical finite-horizon leader trajectory predictions from identical event histories and online correction states. Event-synchronized residual adaptation updates a low-dimensional online correction state at each event to reduce local prediction mismatch. At each valid reference update, reference trajectory replanning uses a quintic connection to join the current reference trajectory to the updated reference trajectory. In multiseed Circle and S-bend missions, the frozen state–residual PINN predictor reduced short-horizon prediction error relative to nominal dynamics rollout, and the residual-adapted predictor reduced it further. Relative to Direct replacement, quintic connection reduced the mean normalized total control variation by 69.70% across 100 missions.

papers.title: Physics-informed semi-supervised LSTM autoencoder framework for force-agnostic structural health monitoring

Traditional model-based SHM approaches offer interpretability and enforce physical laws, while data-driven methods provide flexibility and scalability, yet both face limitations: the former is sensitive to material and modelling uncertainties and often mandates boundary and force information, while the latter relies on extensive labelled datasets and may lack physical consistency. The proposed framework integrates governing physics directly into the LSTM autoencoder and embeds state-space observer principles, enhancing robustness to unknown, time-varying excitations and ensuring stable temporal predictions. A LSTM-based encoder is employed to map the measured accelerations to displacement and health-index estimates, while a physics-based decoder enforces the output-injected state-space dynamics as a training constraint. A semi-supervised training strategy leverages a small, non-exhaustive labelled dataset to guide optimization, improving convergence, stability, and generalization under limited-data conditions. Numerical simulations on a 10-DOF shear building and experimental validations on a four-storey bench-scale frame demonstrate that the framework operates effectively with output-only measurements, detecting, localizing, and quantifying structural damage with sufficient accuracy while maintaining consistency with physical laws. The proposed framework consistently outperforms a force-informed PINN and purely data-driven baselines, remaining reliable under measurement noise, limited training data, and reduced sensor coverage, and the estimated stiffness changes on the bench-scale frame agree with independently measured modal-frequency shifts under both single and multiple brace-removal damage scenarios. It is recognized that the proposed framework offers a computationally efficient and physically consistent route to reliable, input-robust, output-only damage identification. Moreover, this can effectively combine the rigour and interpretability of model-based methods with the adaptability of data-driven approaches within the SHM framework.
