papers.title: Day-ahead BOCNN-LSTM PV prediction based on input of NWP forecasting reconstruction by VMD and CNN-BiGRU-AM network
papers.abstract: Accurate day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for renewable energy scheduling, while the performance is limited by both prediction model and the quality of numerical weather prediction (NWP) information. To address this issue, an integrated two-stage framework is proposed by explicitly coupling NWP error correction with downstream PV power forecasting. The framework separates the correction of meteorological input errors from the learning of the NWP-to-power mapping and generates corrected meteorological variables as intermediate outputs before PV power prediction. This design allows the quality of the corrected NWP inputs and the downstream PV forecasting performance to be evaluated separately, rather than implying universal superiority over end-to-end forecasting architectures. In the first stage, a station-scale NWP correction system based on variational mode decomposition (VMD) and a Convolutional Neural Network Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit Attention Mechanism (CNN-BiGRU-AM) network is developed. The errors sequence between NWP variables and measured meteorological data are decomposed into multiple intrinsic mode functions, which are individually predicted and reconstructed to obtain corrected high-resolution NWP inputs. In the second stage, a Bayesian Optimization Convolutional Neural Network Long Short-Term Memory (BO-CNN-LSTM) model is established for day-ahead PV power forecasting, where Bayesian optimization is used to adaptively determine key hyper-parameters. Four one-month samples that are randomly selected from different seasons are used for validation. The results show that the corrected global horizontal irradiance and temperature both achieve regression coefficient above 0.95, while the corrected wind speed reaches 0.75. Using corrected NWP data as inputs, the proposed framework is evaluated on a 20 MW PV station with a 15 min temporal resolution, corresponding to 96 forecasting points per day. The average RMSE, MAE, and ME are 0.0759 p.u., 0.0580 p.u., and 0.0201 p.u., respectively, where p.u. denotes the normalized value relative to the installed capacity. These values are approximately equivalent to 1.518 MW, 1.160 MW, and 0.402 MW, respectively. The correlation coefficient, accuracy, and qualification rate are 0.9823, 92.41%, and 99.44%, respectively. Further ablation experiments and baseline comparisons indicate that the proposed explicit correction–forecasting framework improves the quality of meteorological inputs and achieves lower day-ahead PV forecasting errors across the four representative seasonal samples considered in this study.

papers.title: IOT-ENABLED PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE FOR CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS IN SAUDI ARABIA: ENHANCING RELIABILITY, EFFICIENCY AND OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE UNDER SAUDI VISION 2030
papers.abstract: Production continuity depends directly on the reliability, efficiency, and recoverability of connected physical assets, on which Saudi Arabia’s industrial diversification and digital transformation increasingly depend. This review critically discusses Internet of Things-enabled predictive maintenance for cyber-physical systems, centering on integrating sensing, edge and cloud computing, machine learning, remaining useful life estimation, digital twins, and maintenance decision support into an operational capability aligned with Vision 2030. We used a structured integrative review approach to synthesize thirty-seven peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and 2025, prioritizing studies from Q1 and Q2 journals. The synthesis shows that predictive maintenance creates value only when accurate models are embedded in a trustworthy end-to-end loop linking condition data, prognosis, operational context, maintenance planning, execution, and learning. The evidence supports temporal deep learning, hybrid and physics-informed prognostics, digital twin-assisted reasoning, and edge analytics but also points out recurring weaknesses such as scarce failure labels, model drift, interoperability, cybersecurity, false alarms, and weak integration with work management. These limitations are additionally exacerbated in the Saudi industrial context by brownfield heterogeneity, severe operating conditions, large asset portfolios, and the need to localize advanced technical capabilities. The review proposes a resilience-oriented architecture and staged deployment roadmap in which asset criticality, secure sensing, model assurance, personnel supervision, enterprise integration, and lifecycle governance are considered interdependent design requirements. It concludes that predictive maintenance aligned with Vision 2030 should be evaluated in terms of operational reliability, maintenance productivity, cyber resilience, workforce capability, and measurable business outcomes rather than predictive accuracy alone.

papers.title: Laser sequence and build orientation govern interface quality in multi-material laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Multi-material laser powder bed fusion (MM-LPBF) offers the ability to locally tailor functional properties by combining dissimilar metals within a single component. However, achieving robust bonding at highly mismatched interfaces remains a critical challenge. This work investigates the interfacial evolution in CuCrZr–316LSS transitions, a material pair with extreme differences in thermal conductivity and a 75% difference in optimal volumetric energy density. This study investigates the interfacial formation mechanisms in CuCrZr–316LSS using five distinct interface configurations: (i) 316L deposited over CuCrZr across a horizontal interface, (ii) CuCrZr deposited over 316L across a horizontal interface, (iii) 316L deposited over CuCrZr along a diagonal interface, (iv) CuCrZr deposited over 316L along a diagonal interface, and (v) the two materials printed with a vertical interface via intralayer deposition. The results demonstrate that deposition order, i.e., laser scanning sequence, and interface geometry critically dictate the quality of interfaces in MM-LPBF systems. Microstructural characterization via optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, electron backscatter diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy revealed that exposure sequence strongly governs interfacial morphology, phase development, and the presence of interfacial defects. To further contextualize these results, meso-scale computational fluid dynamics simulations were employed to capture melt-pool dynamics, convection patterns, and material mixing behavior. Overall, this work clarifies the fundamental role of build orientation and laser scanning sequence in governing process stability and interface quality in MM-LPBF systems (copper- and iron-based in this study) and lays the foundation to achieve reliable interface quality in multi-material components manufactured through MM-LPBF.

Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi performa XGBoost pada prediksi PGK dengan membandingkan model baseline dan model yang dioptimasi menggunakan Bayesian Optimization. Optimasi dilakukan terhadap learning rate, max depth, dan n estimators menggunakan 5-Fold Stratified Cross-Validation dengan mean accuracy sebagai fungsi objektif. Hasil optimasi memperoleh learning rate 0,123745, max depth 3, dan n estimators 318 dengan mean accuracy 97,5%. papers.abstract: The purpose of this research was to investigate the effects of implementing an integrated supervision model to develop teachers’ instructional management competencies: A case study of Wat Phra Koet Khongkharam School. The study employed the G-COSS Integrated Supervision Model, which consists of five steps: 1) Goal Searching (G), identifying goals and development needs; 2) Coordinate Experience (C), coordinating and sharing experiences; 3) Operations Management (O), managing and implementing planned activities; 4) Supervision to Develop (S), providing supervision to develop and enhance teachers’ competencies; and 5) Share to Public (S), sharing knowledge and disseminating the results of implementation. A mixed-methods research approach was employed. The target group consisted of school administrators, teachers, and educational personnel at Wat Phra Koet Khongkharam School. The research instruments comprised a teacher instructional management competency assessment form, a teacher satisfaction questionnaire, and a learner quality assessment form. The research findings revealed that: 1) Following the implementation of the G-COSS Integrated Supervision Model, teachers’ overall instructional management competency was at the highest level ( = 4.66). Teachers were able to design and implement active learning that emphasized learner-centered approaches, appropriately select and utilize instructional media, innovations, and technology, and effectively measure and evaluate learners’ learning outcomes; 2) Teachers’ overall satisfaction with the G-COSS Integrated Supervision Model was at the highest level; 3) Learners’ academic achievement increased after the implementation of the model compared with the previous academic year; and 4) Learners’ key competencies and desirable characteristics showed higher assessment results in all areas. These findings indicate that the G-COSS Integrated Supervision Model is an effective approach for enhancing teachers’ instructional management competencies, supporting their professional development, and improving the quality of learners in a systematic and sustainable manner.
